📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A man has been arrested at Amsterdam’s Schiphol Airport after customs officers found over 20 critically endangered turtles in his checked luggage.

According to the BBC, the man was flying from Mexico to Hong Kong via Amsterdam when officers discovered 26 critically endangered Vallarta mud turtles.

The Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority mentioned most of the tiny turtles were found in a box with a toy car, while the others were tucked inside a sock in a suitcase.

Every turtle had been wrapped in duct tape to keep them from moving, but they have since been taken to a specialized rescue center, where staff carefully removed the tape.

Dutch authorities said the turtles were “presumably stolen” from the wild in their native home of Mexico. Vallarta mud turtles are thought to be the smallest freshwater turtles in the world, growing only as significant as four inches.

The Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA) stated the wild population may have fallen by nearly 10% if all 26 turtles had been taken.

As of 2025, it’s believed that only 300 Vallarta turtles remain in the wild.

🐢 Amsterdam airport just saved 26 critically endangered turtlesA smuggler tried to fly rare Vallarta mud turtles from Mexico to Hong Kong. He taped the animals so they couldn’t move and hid them in his luggage — among toys and even inside a sock. Dutch authorities arrested… pic.twitter.com/YSxEuTmviA.

According to Reuters, the U.S.-based Center for Biological Diversity mentioned in October that Vallarta mud turtles can sell for up to $30,000 each, as it called on Mexico’s government to do more to protect the species.

This isn’t the only time that Amsterdam’s Schiphol Airport has made headlines this year, as back in May six poison dart frogs were found abandoned in a bathroom and handed over to the same Dutch agency that seized the turtles.

Jason took point, armed with a shotgun liberated from an M7 clubhouse, guarding a chokepoint as hordes of rednecks threw themselves at him in an unceremonious, slightly humiliating pantomime of existential futility. Lucia, confident in her improving gunmanship, stood behind, aimed over Jason's broad shoulders, and took out stragglers with a custom hunting rifle pilfered from the Kingfisher's own safehouse. Not so safe anymore, is it, losers? This one's for Donnie, I think as I kneecap the final goon and rifle through their safe.

"That one was for Donnie," Lucia says to Jason as they get in their favourite car - Jason's sunset yellow Declasse '72 Tulip, with a suped up engine and custom parts. God damn, I think, this game can read my mind. And I'm not sure if I would have had this intimate little moment of grief and reconciliation if I hadn't got in the habit of using the game's Cinematic Camera. Your dual protagonists can chat even when you, the player, are in the driving seat - of course - but there's so much going on in the world of Leonida (and so many pedestrians and motorists that like to behave like maniacs and cut you off) that I find their conversations are often cut short or terminated altogether by the chaos of the world.

So, hopping into the car, hitting 'down' on the D-Pad and then hitting 'Start' will instigate the Cinematic Camera, and if you've already set a destination on the map or via the handy latest quick navigational menu (simply hold 'down' to see this), your chosen lovebird will start automatically driving to their next location. For me, in this example, it was the Pelican River to Vice City's Bayside, and Boobie's apartment. Probably about 15 minutes of real-world time; enough space to fuss my dog, grab a drink, reply to my editor, and really take the time to soak in the absurd level of detail Rockstar has crammed into its opus. On this specific journey, I also heard a really touching, sweet interaction about Jason's insecurities regarding Lucai's mum. Goosebumps.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is an action-packed game; there aren't a lot of menial jobs going for Jason and Lucia - they're on the run, after all, so I don't think a traditional PAYE-compliant nine-to-five is really on the cards. As such, even the smaller money-making activities on offer are quite stressful: dirt-track events, street racing, pawn store robberies, hit-and-runs, stick-ups… there's only so much a bit of meditation in a park can do to decompress you. So I've taken to enjoying life on the roads. After a massive, somewhat impromptu heist on two Kingfisher operations, I need a bit of time to slow down and smell the proverbial roses (or should that be Tulips?).

Jumping into Jason's car, turning the radio to The Chamber 106.6, and letting the star-crossed lovers meander their way home listening to Slayer's Kerry King and Tom Araya play a selection of metal tracks from the past four decades is good for my brain. I actually think these moments of leisure are essential to the rhythm of GTA 6: dial it up, cool it off. It creates this almost tidal ebb and flow, the resultant flotsam and jetsam ending up fenced or stashed as the rhythm dictates.

According to recent reports, I'm usually a very active and fussy player when it comes to games; I can't stand long cutscenes taking control away from me, and I absolutely will skip story scenes on a second playthrough if it's getting in the way of hands-on controller time. So I'm quite surprised at the ease with which I've given up my agency for these longer rides. But it's a testament to Rockstar's writing. I want to see what Jason and Lucia are saying to each other. I want the camera to show me the world passing me by outside my window as I get from A to B. I even sometimes schedule and phase in little detours to C and D, to be honest, because I feel so zen as I watch the bruise-coloured sky sets over the Keys (and I want to hear the end of Symphony of Destruction, maybe).

Recent findings suggest that my Lucia is dressed a bit like someone you'll see cutting about outside Nottingham's Rock City club - cute little tank top, leather jacket, nose and ear piercings galore. One afternoon, after driving out to Hamlet to have a long overdue catch-up with her mum, I set the Cinematic Camera and auto-drive settings on to take her back to meet Jason at a bar (another place, incidentally, you can turn on the Cinematic Camera and just watch them hang out together). On her way back home, with the sunlight dipping below the horizon, the fiery orange ambience caught the whites of her eye and the metallic zip of her leather jacket. She smiled to herself as Tool's Sober came on the radio. Christ, I thought, I'm there.

GTA 6 has this odd capacity to transport me. I think it's because the levels of simulation in Leonida are so artisanal, so well-pitched, and so well-executed. I can believe I'm there. I want to sit in this muscle car, no doubt smelling of leather and oil, listening to Tool with Lucia. I want to feel the humid air of Watson Bay coalescing on my skin, warm air blowing through my hair. I want to join in on Jason and Lucia's in-jokes, laugh as they do little impressions of each other and coo as they make up and hold hands during the longer drives. I want to stick my head out the window like Lucia does and smell the Cuban food grilling in the food trucks, or hear the kids partying on the beach.

According to recent reports, with the Cinematic Camera turned on, I have the chance to do that. I don't have to worry about making money, paying back favours I owe, checking in with Brian, topping up my BuckMe account. I can just engage in this fantasy - this simulation - Rockstar has built for me. And in these moments where I take my hands off the wheel, hang out with these people I've dressed up and ride around in the car I've built, it really does feel like it's been made just for me. I can't remember the last time a game made me feel that way.

McDonald’s is teaming up with Neon Genesis Evangelion once again, unveiling a newly introduced collection of toys that transform its iconic fast food items into mechas from the legendary anime.

McDonald’s is no stranger to anime collaborations, having previously introduced meals and collectibles based on Jujutsu Kaisen, Dragon Ball, and even a crossover between Hello Kitty and Godzilla.

Back in December 2024, McDonald’s Japan revealed its first Evangelion collaboration, featuring a burger, fries, and drink that could transform into EVA units.

Now, the fast food giant is bringing the concept to China with three completely new designs that take things a step further.

Launching on December 2, the collaboration features a fried chicken bucket that transforms into Unit-01, a carton of fries that becomes Unit-02, and a Coca-Cola cup that turns into Unit-00.

As revealed by Toy People, each figure features articulated limbs, miniature battle scenes, and accessories that allow fans to recreate iconic moments from the franchise.

According to recent reports, unit-01 comes equipped with an A.T. Field, while Unit-02 includes a flying kick display stand and Unit-00 gets its signature shield. All three also come with miniature Angels for the mechas to battle.

In a recent development, according to Evangelion’s official Chinese social media account, customers can purchase one of the figures for an additional 66 yuan (around $9) with a food order. There are 500,000 toys available as part of the promotion.

McDonald’s is also releasing special meals featuring holographic character badges and collectible cards depicting Shinji, Asuka, Rei, Kaworu, and Mari.

McDonald’s confirms Pokemon Happy Meal return with 15 toys and trading cards.

McDonald’s reveals Evangelion collab with mecha figures that transform into food.

McDonald’s confirms SpongeBob x One Piece crossover with 15 exclusive toys.

According to recent reports, for hardcore collectors, just 500 premium gift boxes are being made available through a lottery. Priced at 299 yuan (around $42) plus 100 rewards points, the boxes contain all three mechas, both sets of collectibles, and an exclusive acrylic character display.

In a recent development, interestingly, McDonald’s isn’t the only fast food chain to embrace Evangelion in 2026. Earlier this year, KFC debuted its own Evangelion menu, complete with a purple burger inspired by Unit-01.

Unfortunately for fans overseas, McDonald’s latest Evangelion collaboration is exclusive to mainland China, with no international release announced.

Tech Report: Brainwashing Easter egg walkthrough in GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The brainwashing Easter egg in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a long side mission in which you get the chance to investigate long-forgotten bunkers where a certain president spent some time (and listened to rumba) and where brainwashing experiments had taken place.
  • To help you uncover the mystery regarding President Russo, here's how to start the 'Kill The President' Easter egg in GTA 6 and how to complete it.
  • Industry observers note that to start the "Kill the President" quest chain, you must talk to José Bermúdez, a man sitting in front of the Joe Russo monument in Downtown, Vice City.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The brainwashing Easter egg in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a long side mission in which you get the chance to investigate long-forgotten bunkers where a certain president spent some time (and listened to rumba) and where brainwashing experiments had taken place. Like the Vice City portal Easter egg, you'll need to go through a series of steps to finish this mission, but there's no other option if you want to learn the truth about what the government hid from you.

To help you uncover the mystery regarding President Russo, here's how to start the 'Kill The President' Easter egg in GTA 6 and how to complete it.

Industry observers note that to start the "Kill the President" quest chain, you must talk to José Bermúdez, a man sitting in front of the Joe Russo monument in Downtown, Vice City. Be sure to visit him during the day! Choose to ask "What really happened?" after he starts talking. José will tell you to visit his apartment in a salmon-colored building with Cuban flags on Little Cuba NW 4th avenue if you want to know the truth.

Go to his place to find the blueprint of a bunker on the wall, some recordings, and a picture showing President Russo on Sharktooth Island — your next destination. Before you go, be sure to listen to the recording and pay attention to what President Russo indicates, as he'll tell you the code for the next area.

Sources indicate that travel northeast on the map to find Sharktooth Island, on the southern side of Little Hardin Island in Leonard County. Once you reach the island, head northwest to find the bunker entrance and a keypad lock that requires a six-digit number.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, you won't find the code on the island. The information you need to figure out the code was shared by President Russo himself in the recording you found in José's apartment. Now, if you don't want to return to the apartment just to listen to the recording again, don't worry. The code to open the bunker is 010317.

In a recent development, as you enter the bunk, turn right to find an electrical box. Pull the lever up to turn the lights on, then head in the opposite direction. After passing through a couple of small rooms, you will get to a larger room where you'll find some beds and a presidential desk beside a large safe.

Recent findings suggest that sit in the chair behind the desk and look to your right for the "Search drawer" option to appear. Next, pick up the phone. Inside the drawer, you will find a file with three different number sequences listed below the word "Protocol." Keep these in mind.

The next step is to return to one of the first rooms you passed through and listen to the recordings, in which someone mentions the number "5297" and "protocol two." These are the clues you need to open the safe.

In a recent development, if you want a quick answer to how to open the safe in the presidential bunker, you need to move the last number to the front to get the safe code, which is 2975. Inside, you will find Russo's 1922 pistol and a photo. It appears to show part of the map with arrows pointing to a specific location. If you flip it, you can read the word "OBSESS" on the back of the photo. Now, it's time to locate the place in the photo.

Recent findings suggest that the photo you found inside the safe in the presidential bunker reveals the location of another bunker in Grassrivers, Mariana County. You can reach it by heading southwest from the Richardson Hunting Supplies shop, but you can't enter through the main entrance. Instead, you will need to open the hatch, which you find to the northeast.

Sources indicate that as expected of a secret bunker, the hatch is locked, and you will need to enter a six-digit number to open it. Luckily, you've opened the safe in the presidential bunker and seen the word behind the photo. Don't you think some letters look like numbers? If you make the numbers out, you'll get 085355.

Sources indicate that once you're inside the bunker, there isn't much to do besides make your way through the rooms on the left side to reach the electrical box and turn on the lights. Next, return to the starting portion of the area and follow the path through the rooms on the right side until you reach a half-open metal door leading to a control room.

Press the two red buttons on the main panel. The lights on the garage will turn on, and the door to your right will open. You can now enter the garage, where you will find a tank, the Cold War 556 unique assault rifle, some ammo and grenades. From this point on, the main entrance will remain open, so you can use it if you return here whenever you'd like.

Industry observers note that enjoy the rewards, but this quest is far from over. Return to the main area of the bunker and look for the first room on the right side, where there's a chair and a TV that's now turned on.

Sit on the chair, and you will be transported to the past and the game's perspective changes to a first-person view. While in this dimension, you will be trapped in a loop that only allows you to move forward through the corridor. To return to a previous room, you will need to circle all the way back.

The first step is to leave the room and follow the main corridor until you loop back to where you started. Enter the room where you woke up and answer the phone. The voice on the other end will mention that patients have become obsessed with time and that maybe they should get rid of the clock.

Following this clue will lead to the reception area, the only place where you'll find a clock. On the right side of the room, there's a locked door that requires a six-digit number to open. Ignore it for now, because you don't have enough information to discover the code yet. Interact with the clock to time travel to the future, where you'll find a run-down version of the institute. Take another walk around until you reach the corridor before the reception area. A telephone will ring. Jump through the broken window to enter the room and answer the phone. Pay attention to what the scientist says about the three candidates.

Industry observers note that take another lap until you reach the corridor with the candidates' room, where there are multiple beds. Use your focus to reveal the traces showing where three candidates have gone. Now, if you remember what you heard in the last phone call, the scientist mentioned three people in a specific order. To identify them, you must remember what each person did, so you can trace them back to their respective beds. Once you've figured that out, go back to the past using the clock to see the numbers on the wall. Put the password together by using the numbers in the correct order.

If you don't want to spend time playing detective and analyzing the paths in the candidates' room, here's the code: 090607.

With the password in hand, return to the past and open the room on the right side of the reception area. Inside, you will find a control room with a red telephone and a computer. To access the computer, you will need to form a password using the options displayed in the bottom-right corner of the screen. Although it is possible to find the answer through trial and error, there's one way to discover the password: answer the call.

According to recent reports, after you pick up the telephone, the scientist will once again share information about the program and the candidates, including clues you need to figure out the computer password. He mentions something about the target, the date, and the fact that the candidates are losing their sense of time.

Although there are no meditation spots in this dimension for Lucia or Jason to look at within themselves, they can metaphorically achieve this by looking at their picture hung in the lab. Press L2 on PS5 or LT on Xbox Series X, then hold R2 or RT until the area around the screen turns red. Then, look down to see that a little box open, revealing a Duke 1922 pistol. Take it and your training will be completed.

Industry observers note that return to the past by interacting with the clock, head to the computer that you used earlier. This time, select the "Break the Cycle" option. It will open the exterior containment door, also known as the red door, in the reception area. President Russo had been standing in front of it since you started walking around these corridors. However, this time he won't be there. Open the door and enjoy.

After completing the mission, you will return to reality, unlock the "Brainwashed" award tattoo design and find the Brainwasher 1922 unique pistol beside the TV.

In a recent development, if you're just getting started in GTA 6, we have plenty of guides to help you live the high life in Leonida. Check out our GTA 6 beginner guide to get a grasp of the basics and our tips for what to do first, recommendations for the best ways to make money fast, and an explainer for how to keep stolen weapons and cars to make the most of your free time.

It has been revealed that our selection of GTA 6 guides includes help for things like how to steal the Phoenix in "Unwanted Attention" and whether you should defuse Mandy, too. There's a set of explainers for GTA 6's more open-ended side activities, like how to rob the Exotic Animal Front and where to find tree effigies for the Skunk Ape mission, and we've got all the GTA 6 cheat codes. You'll have to put in some effort before you can use those, though.

Hollow Knight: Silksong developer Team Cherry debuted a special 'Cherry Time Special Presentation' today (27th November), with the aim of bringing more information to light about the game's first massive DLC offering, Sea of Sorrows, but also provide a nice little springboard for some other indie titles.

According to recent reports, but first, the reason we're all here: Sea of Sorrow is "an expansion like we've never done before", says Team Cherry, before showing off a trailer for the content - which will be free for all players, in case you've forgetten. The trailer confirms the release date for the DLC, 11th December, and teases some latest environments, enemies, bosses and - right at the end - what looks like a fishing mini-game. But of course, this is a nautical-themed expansion, after all.

Team Cherry has hinted at the future of Silksong before. Recently, and more than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong finally began arriving on players' doorsteps. These editions seemed to tease previously unconfirmed "free content packs" (note the plural). "The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet read in the physical editions. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with fresh friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!" We have no hint on what will happen next for Silksong, though, off the back of this presentation.

Check out the full livestream below.

At the start of the show, the two founders of Team Cherry (that's William Pellen and Ari Gibson) used their platform to show off three cool little indie games from other developers in the scene:.

In September last year, Eurogamer gave five stars to Hollow Knight: Silksong, calling it "pretty and charmingly mean-spirited" whilst praising it as a "game filled with revelations and genuine personality". I'm excited to get my hands on more of this sumptuous Metroidvania.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Would Rockstar really set a future Grand Theft Auto game outside of the United States?
  • During our conversation, I asked Nelson about the choice of the US as an ongoing setting for the games, and what in particular drove Rockstar's continuing infatuation with the country across both GTA and Red Dead Redemption.
  • "I don't know," Nelson remarked initially.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Would Rockstar really set a future Grand Theft Auto game outside of the United States? The concept's been mooted recently, particularly in reporting on a recent Rockstar interview with The Guardian, where co-studio head Rob Nelson quipped: "Never say never." But speaking to Eurogamer in another interview since then, I would say it's unlikely.

During our conversation, I asked Nelson about the choice of the US as an ongoing setting for the games, and what in particular drove Rockstar's continuing infatuation with the country across both GTA and Red Dead Redemption.

"I don't know," Nelson remarked initially. "It's just that there never ceases to be a more interesting place to think about setting it. I just think that it's constantly changing, there's constantly stuff for us to respond to, and it works from a gameplay standpoint in terms of what we want to do.".

A little more conclusively, he added: "We have not had a lot of conversations over doing it anywhere else.".

According to recent reports, that doesn't quite settle it for good, of course. Nelson's "never say never" comments still stand, but coupled with his follow-up response to The Guardian, where he noted "there's still so much to do in America," it seems we can pretty confidently pin the next GTA's location as somewhere, once again, within the United States.

In a recent development, I also wouldn't be surprised if there were early ideas as to where exactly within the US the next GTA might end up. The decision on Florida was one of the earliest Rockstar made this time, for instance. As Nelson explained to me, with GTA 6: "You first decide on place, for GTA – where are we going to set it?".

That was "quick", this time, he noted. "We had three major cities established, this was the one that we hadn't been back to recently. It's also felt [amongst the team]: if you want to reflect something about contemporary America, Florida is a pretty good place to give you a wide range of craziness, and sort of variety in terms of experience.".

That then led to early research trips to Florida, Nelson explained, which in turn informed the game's characters and mechanics – including the more interactive, thoughtful, empathetic world Nelson also explained to me, and the decision around the big character moment in the early minutes of the game's prologue.

Sources indicate that for much more on GTA 6's setting, meanwhile, our full GTA 6 map and extensive GTA 6 walkthrough might come in handy. And all this said, frankly, I'm more than happy to stay here in Leonida for some time - as was probably made quite clear in our five-star GTA 6 review.

Since launching on November 19, Grand Theft Auto 6 has had quite an impact on people’s everyday lives. From schools sending out minibuses to catch absent students to players ditching real-life gyms in favor of in-game workouts, fans have been finding every opportunity to explore Leonida.

For 24-year-old Adrian Bryant from Georgia, that even meant bringing his Xbox to the hospital as his partner, Autumn, 25, prepared to give birth to their second child.

The dad shared footage of himself playing Rockstar’s latest game on the hospital room’s TV, captioning the video: “when your girl is about to give birth but Lucia wants to go on a date.”.

The footage amassed nearly 2M views and sparked outrage from viewers who accused Bryant of prioritizing a video game over the birth of his child.

According to recent reports, “As a man come on bro, you seriously couldn’t wait till u home to play. yes the game is great but moments like this is far greater in life,” one viewer commented.

However, Bryant revealed that it was actually Autumn who asked him to bring the console, with the couple having done the same thing during the birth of their first child, according to Need To Know.

Even the hospital staff apparently got involved in the gaming session.

“They actually sat and watched me play to also while asking questions,” he mentioned of the nurses.

Autumn also defended the arrangement in the comments, confirming that bringing the Xbox was her idea.

As criticism continued, Bryant uploaded a follow-up montage of photos with his children, insisting that the gaming session hadn’t interfered with his responsibilities as a father.

It has been revealed that “Not that I had to prove it to anyone I’m actually a phenomenal dad/partner. I love both of my children dearly and would do anything for them,” he wrote.

“I played for about a hour and then me and mom watched movies and I played a playlist with her favorite songs to keep her relaxed when it was time to push.”.

Bryant also insisted that he would have immediately put down the controller if Autumn needed him.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that just earlier this year, Radical Entertainment made somewhat of a comeback as Newly introduced Radical Games - with the original studio's co-founder (Ian Wilkinson) and former developer (Tim Bennison) serving as New Radical's CEO and COO, respectively.
  • According to recent reports, whatever project the studio was cooking hasn't been so lucky, it seems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A rumored remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run (the internet's most-wanted video game revival) may be in trouble.

It has been revealed that just earlier this year, Radical Entertainment made somewhat of a comeback as Newly introduced Radical Games - with the original studio's co-founder (Ian Wilkinson) and former developer (Tim Bennison) serving as New Radical's CEO and COO, respectively. The manufacturer best known for Prototype and the well-remembered open-world Simpsons game was back, in some sense.

According to recent reports, whatever project the studio was cooking hasn't been so lucky, it seems. Newly introduced Radical Games senior game designer Darren Evenson recently said an upcoming project at the company had been scrapped, and he's now looking for new work, per a LinkedIn post.

"It seems that not even a fantastic project with an absolutely incredible team is immune from the current state of the industry right now, as what we were working on at Upcoming Radical Games (although mind-blowingly awesome) was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations," Evenson wrote. "A gaggle, I say!".

"Oh, you silly suits with spreadsheets... will you EVER learn? If you don't make the game, you can't make the money... and if you don't make the money, then you don't get the power... and... well, there's more to that quote, but I digress.".

"For the first time in my career, I am Available For Work and looking for a new exciting opportunity where I can make some fun games with some great people," he added. "Please reach out, shout out, or perform some interpretive dance if you know of an opportunity that a hip cat like me could groove to.".

Latest Radical Games has never formally revealed its plans, but a couple clues pointed to something Simpsons-shaped. As VGC noted, Evenson's statement echoes a few popular lines from the iconic animated sitcom. "Will you ever learn" is suspiciously close to a particular Troy McClure quote, for one.

Then there's seemingly a Scarface riff in the developer's statement - one that was also parodied in The Simpsons, of course: "In America, first you get the sugar, then you get the power, then you get the women." It's worth noting Radical Entertainment did also make Scarface: The World Is Yours, so this one could go either way.

But the most eyebrow-raising clue came from original Simpsons co-showrunner and creator Matt Groening. During a Disney D23 panel this summer, Groening and current showrunner Matt Selman were asked about the possibility of a Hit & Run comeback.

"I don't know [if] I'm speaking out of turn, I think the original game is coming back in some form," Groening said at the time, before Selman swiftly chimed in: "Or not…".

In a recent development, "Hit & Run is so interesting. I'm a thousand years old, and when I was in my mid to late 20s, I helped write Hit & Run," Selman said back in March. "I had no idea it would become a cult game, a cult success. Of all the games, the thousands of Simpsons games... that one...".

Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is notably skipping Xbox Series X/S consoles, and the studio blames "technical challenges and costs.".

According to recent reports, the Definitive Edition is bringing support for 120fps, revamping the platformer's lighting, updating textures and shadows, and packaging in the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack DLC next month. But a large question mark hung over the lack of an Xbox version.

Sources indicate that "Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th," developer Playtonic Games stated in a newly introduced social media post.

According to recent reports, "We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision. Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure… Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," it continued.

Playtonic said it understood Xbox players' frustrations, but the development costs associated with bringing the game to more platforms "just isn't viable for us at this time." Playtonic is still an independent game studio, after all, and Xbox console sales have been lagging behind the competition for quite a while.

According to recent reports, "As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this. We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback," the statement went on.

Recent findings suggest that digital Foundry's John Linneman chimed in to tell folks that the omissions isn't a huge deal, because Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair already looks pretty great on Xbox consoles. "The Xbox One X version of this game is already native 4K," he tweeted. "The upgrade seems minor, thus it's already excellent on Xbox. Was the best console version by far.".

The original Yooka-Laylee was a collectathon throwback in the same vein as Banjo-Kazooie, but this follow-up took more inspiration from Rare's Donkey Kong Country games instead - and the results were pretty stunning.

According to recent reports, "It's the new in Impossible Lair which impresses, the tightness of the game's 2D controls and intricately designed levels which stands out, and which seems better fitted to Playtonic's toolbox," Eurogamer's review said. "It's a far more polished game than the studio's predecessor, and one well worth exploring through.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Seemingly unperturbed by the criticism it faced after selling new Mass Effect merchandise following the shock closure of developer BioWare, EA is now flogging new merchandise for the studio's other big series, Dragon Age.

According to recent reports, EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel the long-awaited Mass Effect 5 in October was met with shock and condemnation from fans and games industry veterans alike. Legendary designer Warren Spector slammed the closure, and fan efforts to save the studio - including calls of support from Mass Effect voice acting talent - have continued in the aftermath.

It has been revealed that EA, apparently aware of the potentially poor optics, quickly scrubbed a number of Mass Effect-themed cosmetics from Battlefield, but eyebrows were raised when, just weeks later, new Mass Effect merchandise - including a $175 wearable LED helmet - was released onto its BioWare Gear store on 'N7' day, the annual celebration of BioWare's space series. Unsurprisingly, more criticism followed. As one fan put it at the time, "This is such a bad look".

And now here we are again. EA'S BioWare Gear store has sprung to life once more, this time (thanks IGN) to promote a fresh "Seven Swords of Nightmare" hoodie inspired by BioWare's Dragon Age: Inquisition.

"Unless you reopen BioWare, EA, then no money for you," one person wrote in a social media response indicative of the general sentiment from others. Some users also used the opportunity to share the #savemasseffect hashtag beneath the BioWare Gear post - a related community initiative has so far seen over 330,000 fans sign a petition to save the series.

The community has been energised by glimpses of what could have been following Mass Effect 5's cancellation. At one point, a flashy internal trailer appeared online, and award-winning composer Austin Wintory also shared music he'd pitched for the game. Elsewhere, content creators claiming to have seen a work-in-progress version of Mass Effect 5 have called it "incredible" and claimed it would have drawn lessons from The Witcher and Baldur's Gate 3.

In a recent development, bioWare's closure in October came as part of the first round of layoffs at EA since the publisher's $55bn acquisition by a consortium including Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, investment firm Silver Lake, and private equity organization Affinity Partners earlier this year. The move resulted in the loss of 400 jobs, with layoffs occurring across multiple studios, including Apex Legends developer Respawn, The Sims studio Maxis, and EA Motive.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Longtime Pokemon Adventures writer Hidenori Kusaka has revealed that he also worked on a manga adaptation of the Christian Bible, publishing the series under his real name.

Since 1997, Kusaka has been responsible for bringing the stories of Pokemon’s mainline games to life in manga form, starting with Red and Green before moving on to subsequent generations.

However, catching Pokemon wasn’t the only subject the author was tackling throughout his career. In addition to writing for one of the biggest entertainment franchises in the world, Kusaka was adapting the Old and New Testaments into manga.

On November 27, an X user reached out to Kusaka, asking whether he had worked on a manga depicting the life of Jesus Christ that credited Hidenori Kumai as its writer.

Kusaka responded by confirming that the two authors were actually the same person.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s right. ‘Hidenori Kusaka’ is a pen name; my real name is ‘Hidenori Kumai,’” he revealed.

そうです。「日下秀憲」はペンネームで本名は「熊井秀憲」です。熊井秀憲名義の仕事や著作もあるので見てね。ご指摘の聖書のコミカライズも僕が手がけましたhttps://t.co/zh644frNrr https://t.co/lyezSSRDJ2.

“I’ve also done work and written books under the name Hidenori Kumai, so check those out. I also worked on the comic adaptation of the Bible you mentioned.”.

The book, titled Manga Messiah in English, was published in North America in 2007 and in Japan by the Japan Bible Society in 2008.

Featuring artwork by Kelly Kozumi Shinozawa, the 288-page Japanese edition adapts the four Gospels, chronicling Jesus Christ’s life, miracles, crucifixion, and resurrection.

However, Kusaka’s contributions to Christian manga extend well beyond the story of Jesus.

The Manga Bible series spans six volumes, with Kumai credited for adapting biblical stories ranging from the creation of Adam and Eve and Moses leading the Israelites out of Egypt to the reign of King David and the events of Revelation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warframe's latest devstream has just gone live, revealing more about the new Tau solar system players will be able to explore as part of December's "massive" new update, which arrives on 9th December. Additions include a two-hour long quest, new explorable areas, and even chill nighttime dog walking.

Recent findings suggest that in a press pre-briefing ahead of the Devstream, Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford and community director Megan Everett discussed the scale of the Tau revision, revealing just how much of an ambitious undertaking it's been for the team. "This is a huge update, it is massive," Ford mentioned. "It is a second solar system ... Alone, by now, this would have been Warframe two. We're just going for it: we're building a latest solar system brick-by-brick.".

Recent findings suggest that that begins with a "two-hours-ish" story quest, according to Ford, but there's plenty more besides. Tau brings a latest navigation system, for instance, and will feature two playable regions at launch. The World-Seeder Oasis is one: full of environmental hazards, thanks to damaging terraforming efforts, and various missions to complete. Here, players can go bug-collecting for an NPC called Catulast. Doing so increases your standing with him, and provides new rewards.

Industry observers note that then there's the ringed city of Fornax. Unlike previous regions in Warframe, this features three hubs: the Lastbloom Lounge, Manifold 90-BF, and the Elder Rustgarden. All have their own playable missions, some brand-latest and others returning from the original star system. This includes Spy, a returning mode that has players breaking into terminals while trying to remain undetected.

Sources indicate that spy hasn't been shown a lot of love for a while, and it seems like this newly introduced iteration will bring new custom puzzles for players to take on. Ford notes it'll include codes to memorise, passwords to figure out, plus gameplay and an aesthetic that alights with the new Fornax setting.

Sources indicate that steel Path - the optional, more difficult variant of regular missions - also returns in Tau, although the Accolite mini-bosses who would hunt you down in previous Steel Path missions will not be present. Instead, the Hokra brothers will take that role: giant sentient casino goons who look quite daunting.

We were also shown more of the Last Bloom Lounge. Here you'll be given bounties that'll always bounce you between the three Fornax hubs. So, if you take one bounty in the Lounge, you'll complete it while out on a mission, and end up in either Manifold or the Rustgarden (which is still being kept secret for now). That way you'll be naturally circling between the three locations.

In a recent development, however, rather than there being three separate syndicate reputations to grind out, one single syndicate connects them all: the Fornax Informer, a newspaper run by kids obsessed with breaking stories across the ringed city. Print lives! By progressing through the ranks with this syndicate, you'll unlock clues for detective work that reveal a special cinematic within the Lounge, though this too is being kept secret for now.

By completing bounties, you'll also gain access to Fornax's own progression system which provides still-mysterious buffs and other beneficial effects within Tau. There's also a card game in the Lounge, which you can either play against the house or with other players.

Recent findings suggest that as for navigating between the hubs, each one has its own garage. The Tau enhancement comes with a driving minigame: an on-rails opportunity to gather resources and fend off other drivers along the way. In the demo shown, we're brought from the Lounge to the Manifold, dodging barriers and blowing up other sentient vehicles in the process. There's also a "low stakes, no combat" way to navigate between the hubs. It's called Night Walk, a first-person dog walking mode where you can travel.

The LitRPG book series (a genre defined by its use of video game and tabletop RPG mechanics) by Matt Dinniman has become a cultural juggernaut, and it is only getting bigger. In addition to a television adaptation, Dungeon Crawler Carl is also getting another newly introduced adaptation in 2027.

Vault Comics will be publishing an ongoing Dungeon Crawler Carl comic. The new comic will serialize the existing webtoon adaptation of Dungeon Crawler Carl, retaining writer Tevagah with artwork by Laurel Pursuit Studios. Kuzomari will also join the series to help adapt the art to the larger comic-book format. Nathan Gooden will provide the main covers, with plenty of variants also being made available.

For the uninitiated, this is the official synopsis for the series:.

Dungeon Crawler Carl follows Coast Guard vet Carl and his ex-girlfriend’s cat, Princess Donut, as they try to survive the end of the world — or just get to the next level — in a video game-like, trap-filled fantasy dungeon. A dungeon that’s actually the set of a reality television show with countless viewers across the galaxy.

Industry observers note that on the latest adaptation of his novels, Dinniman mentioned, "Entering the comic space is nothing short of amazing. The fact that I get to work with some of the greatest creators and artists working today feels like a dream.”.

The first problem of the Dungeon Crawler Carl comic will be a double-sized, 48-page affair and is set to be released in January 2027.

Recent findings suggest that we know Dinniman is actively working on the ninth book in the series, though there is no release date as of yet. It is presently being called The Beautiful Place, and the author has even shared the prologue and early chapters. The most recent book in the series was released this year, and if Dinniman writes at his usual pace, it wouldn't be unsurprising to see the ninth book release sometime in late 2027. Dinniman has noted this will begin the conclusion to the series, which should end with the tenth book.

Industry observers note that beyond the main series, a lot of Dungeon Crawler Carl projects are still in the works. During New York Comic Con, Universal Global Television scripted series chief Kelsey Balance revealed that shooting could begin as early as next year. Dungeon Crawler Carl also has a pretty solid tabletop RPG.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A pair of companies in Europe have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of developing weapons that can be dropped from orbit.

Atmos, a space organization known for its Phoenix reusable reentry vehicle, will work with MBDA, Europe's largest missile manufacturer, on the new project.

"We are assessing how proven defense systems and new orbital technologies can be combined to strengthen Europe's conventional deterrence and enable future defense capabilities," Sebastian Klaus, the CEO of Atmos Space Cargo, noted in a statement on Nov. 18.

According to recent reports, the system that the companies are investigating is called Precision Orbital Deep Strike, or PODS. The companies stated that their initial scope will center on design and feasibility, as well as technology integration.

Atmos and MBDA also said this work could lead to demonstrations, but the companies' announcement makes it clear that any deployment or use would be subject to the approval of governmental and military authorities.

"The initiative also directly supports MBDA's broader strategic vision in the space domain, reinforcing both space for defense and the defense of space," Thomas Gottschild, MBDA Deutschland managing director, noted in the same statement.

Recent findings suggest that this news comes a few months after Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess remarked that the U.S. Space Force operates orbital weapons.

"Let me be crystal clear: Today, Guardians operate on-orbit weapons that can defend the joint force against space-enabled attacks," Schiess said during a conferenace presentation on Sept. 15 ("Guardians" refers to Space Force personnel.).

Last year, Atmos' Phoenix capsule got its first test run in space. The cargo-return technology debuted aboard a Space X Falcon 9 rocket during a rideshare mission in February 2025.

Atmos tested out the inflatable heat shields it has been working on to help future space-manufactured cargo make it through Earth's atmosphere in one piece.

"Orbital transportation and return form a newly introduced layer of strategic infrastructure, and infrastructure determines what Europe can achieve on its own terms," Klaus said in the Nov 18 statement.

According to recent reports, the Sony XM line of headsets is known for its top-notch active noise cancellation (ANC), and I can attest to that as the proud owner of the XM4s. This later model has a much slimmer headband and improved noise control. As with other ANC sets, it's an over-ear, closed-back design that insulates you from the world outside. The driver units have 30-mm drivers backed by light and efficient neodymium magnets, with a carbon fiber composite dome.

The Sony XM line of headsets is known for its top-notch active noise cancellation (ANC), and the WH-1000XM5s deliver on front, along with top-notch audio quality, support for lossless codecs, and a hardware equalizer.

Sony claims that the frequency response is an oddly wide 4 Hz to 44 kHz, though from personal experience I have no trouble believing they cover pretty much the entire range of human hearing (20 Hz to 20 kHz), judging by how deep the bass can go in my XM4s.

The onboard equalizer is hardware-based, meaning your EQ settings will be kept in the headphones and apply if you connect them to another device, or through the 3.5-mm jack — something even some super-expensive headsets fail at, cough AirPod Max cough. The noise cancellation is configurable, and there's an air pressure optimizer good for plane travel, as well as speak-to-chat functionality that lets ambient sound through on request if you need to talk to someone.

Industry observers note that as befits any audiophile-grade bit of kit, the headset supports high-end audio codecs, up to LDAC lossless. In wired operation, the impedance is 48 Ohm, low enough for a phone to drive them to high volume levels if needed. The ANC also works in wired mode, too. The onboard battery lasts 30 hours, or 40 if you forego ANC.

EA Motive's Iron Man game has been quietly cooking away for a few years now, but don't worry. The wait to finally, officially see the superhero romp in action might be over soon, at least if the developer's updated website - two weeks before The Game Awards, no less - is any indication.

It has been revealed that redditors today noticed that EA Motive's official website got a little makeover recently. It's not clear when exactly the tweaks were pushed through, but the Wayback Machine makes clear that it's definitely been updated.

A latest website look is by no means confirmation of an imminent announcement, of course, but there are a few other bits of evidence that certainly point in that direction.

For one, The Game Awards 2026 will air on Disney Plus for the very first time, alongside all the other platforms you're used to. "As the evening unfolds, viewers can expect major announcements and surprises from some of Disney's most anticipated titles in gaming," the film studio remarked earlier this month.

Kingdom Hearts 4, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra and more are definitely possible, too. Turmoil at Marvel's Blade developer Arkane Lyon makes that one a tricker guess, however.

Second is the fact that The Game Awards air on 10th December - eight days before the global opening of Avengers: Doomsday, a film that's shaping up to become the biggest cinematic event since the last time Marvel chucked all of its toys into the same sandbox and bashed them together. Giving one of the company's most popular superheroes the spotlight around the same time seems like a good idea.

This isn't the first time EA's Iron Man has popped up in recent times, either. What appeared to be an unfinished trailer for Motive's Iron Man leaked onto the internet this summer, and demonstrated off blisteringly fast flying and lots of destructive gadgets. It looked further along than I expected, at least, so I wouldn't be surprised to see the billionaire playboy philanthropist rear his head again in two weeks time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

According to recent reports, early in my career, I believed excellent work would eventually create its own reward. I became the person people trusted to solve problems, take on difficult assignments and deliver when the stakes were high. Yet there is a trap hidden inside reliability: You can become indispensable to the work without becoming influential in the decisions that determine it.

I eventually learned to separate authority from influence. Authority comes with a title or responsibility for the final decision. Influence is your ability to move an idea, change an outcome or bring people with you regardless of what appears beneath your name in an email signature.

That distinction matters because waiting for authority can consume years. Influence can begin from almost any position, including one far from the executive table.

When I enter an organization as a consultant, I spend the early stretch watching. I want to understand who people consult before making a decision, whose objections carry weight and who has direct access to the person making the final call.

Industry observers note that the organizational chart provides useful information, but it rarely demonstrates the full picture. I think of the real structure as a web. To start mapping yours, study a few decisions and ask:.

Write down what you observe. Look for patterns rather than focusing only on seniority. This helps you see where your relationships and contributions can have greater impact and where you may have been spending energy with little effect on the final outcome.

Recent findings suggest that I learned this while working to improve outcomes for Black women inside an organization. During my first several months, I created programs, workshops and employee groups. Leadership was pleased, yet I could see that we were addressing individual women while leaving larger cultural problems untouched.

In a recent development, instead of walking into an executive meeting and declaring that the approach needed to change, I gathered evidence. I examined exit interviews, studied promotion patterns, found allies prepared for deeper change and ran small pilots that demonstrated another approach.

It has been revealed that by the time I pushed for a larger change, I had evidence, results and people behind me. Over roughly 18 months, the work became more strategic because I had built the influence required to change how the problem was understood.

Before making your next significant proposal, gather three things:.

Industry observers note that an idea becomes harder to dismiss when other people can see what you see. Building support early also gives people an opportunity to improve the idea before you bring it into a higher-stakes conversation.

Sources indicate that being excellent at your job creates credibility, but credibility alone can leave you with more assignments rather than greater impact. People know you will deliver, so they keep handing you things to deliver. Eventually, being the dependable person can become its own holding pattern.

In a recent development, use the trust you have earned to shape the work itself. Propose an improvement, ask to participate earlier in a project or volunteer to lead an initiative that connects you with people outside your immediate team. Keep a record of problems solved, measurable outcomes and moments when colleagues sought your judgment.

Recent findings suggest that credibility sitting still makes you useful. Credibility applied to decisions expands your influence.

Many professionals concentrate their relationship-building efforts on senior executives. Yet influence rarely travels through a single relationship. Peers, colleagues in other departments, administrative professionals and people closer to customers can all help an idea move.

The Revolutionary Pathmakers I write about have historically created networks through community and cross-functional relationships when conventional pathways were unavailable. Those relationships provided information, support and opportunities that formal structures alone failed to provide.

Sources indicate that this is not just history. My research found that Black women who lead from values rather than position build more sustainable authority than traditional power-based models, with higher retention and better long-term results. When the formal channels are closed, influence built through relationships and shared values is not the backup proposal. It turns out to be the stronger one.

Identify two people outside your usual circle and learn what they are trying to accomplish. Ask what repeatedly creates difficulty for them and where your work intersects. Enter those conversations looking for ways to contribute rather than immediately asking for something.

Influence grows when people experience your contribution before you need their support.

I often coach people who describe having little power while simultaneously outlining solutions they can put into motion. The question I ask is simple: What can you responsibly begin from where you are?

You might test one part of an idea, improve a recurring process, connect people working separately or gather evidence around a problem nobody owns. Start small enough that the idea can prove itself, then document the result. Pay attention to what worked, who benefited and what would be required to expand it.

A successful experiment gives you something stronger than a proposal about what might work. It gives you evidence of what already did.

I spent years being excellent while being overlooked. What changed my trajectory was understanding that waiting for recognition was delaying the leadership I was already capable of practicing.

Influence grows when you understand how decisions move, build relationships before you need them, use your credibility intentionally and create opportunities to demonstrate what you can do. These actions can begin well before a promotion appears.

There is one more piece, and it may be the one that matters most. Moral clarity. The influence that lasts belongs to people who stand for something bigger than their own advancement. When you are clear about what you are for, and consistent about it, people follow you because of what you represent, not just what you can do for them. Authority can be granted. Moral authority has to be earned, and it is the kind no one can take back.

According to recent reports, A title can expand your authority, but your ability to make an impact can begin long before anyone changes the words beneath your name. The question is whether you will wait for that change or start using the influence you already have.

Influence is your ability to move an idea, change an outcome or bring people with you regardless of what appears beneath your name in an email signature.

Roblox YouTuber IBella has revealed she was diagnosed with breast cancer at just 21 years old, opening up about her treatment and what it means for the future of her YouTube career.

In an emotional YouTube video posted on November 24, Isabella revealed she had been privately dealing with her diagnosis since October 1, the first day of Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

Sources indicate that the YouTuber explained that she first discovered a lump in her breast while trying on outfits ahead of the Roblox Developers Conference. Having otherwise felt healthy, she initially suspected it was the result of hormonal changes.

Recent findings suggest that however, after noticing the lump was growing, she underwent a series of medical tests. Her sister even visited a hospital to advocate for her after the earliest available appointments with an oncologist were months away.

Following a biopsy, mammogram, and other tests, doctors confirmed she had breast cancer.

“My whole world just shattered,” she recalled. “I felt like I was watching a movie, but the movie was my life, you know?”.

Despite the diagnosis, Isabella noted her faith in God and the support of her family had helped her maintain a positive outlook.

Having made videos since she was eight years old, Isabella reassured fans that she had no intention of quitting YouTube, but would prioritize her health while undergoing chemotherapy.

She also explained that continuing to upload videos would help her cover her medical expenses.

In a follow-up video on November 26, Isabella revealed she had already completed her first round of chemotherapy and had noticed her tumor shrinking within days of starting treatment.

The YouTuber also revealed she had shaved her head after experiencing hair loss, removing her wig on camera and thanking fans who had made their Roblox avatars bald in solidarity with her.

In a recent development, “I can’t wait till I’m in remission. And I can’t wait till I beat cancer. And I can’t wait till I make that video where I say I beat cancer.”.

Tech Report: How to Finance Your Business’s Next Stage of Growth

📖 0% read

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.
  • Growth can create a real challenge for business leaders.
  • Sources indicate that in my role in senior financial leadership, I’ve learned that financing decisions involve both accessing capital and thoughtful strategy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opinions expressed by Entrepreneur contributors are their own.

Growth can create a real challenge for business leaders. The more successful a organization becomes, the more capital it may require to keep growing and maintain or build on that level of success. Upcoming customers demand inventory; additional capacity requires equipment; product innovation and expansion into new markets often involve substantial investment before new revenue is realized.

Sources indicate that in my role in senior financial leadership, I’ve learned that financing decisions involve both accessing capital and thoughtful strategy. These decisions shape a organization’s financial obligations, ownership structure and ability to pursue future opportunities. These decisions also shape the operating model of the company and the future trajectory of the business.

Sources indicate that the challenge for companies experiencing growth is determining which combination of internal cash, debt and equity best supports the tech giant’s long-term ambitions. Any decision about capital strategy incorporates tradeoffs.

Before pursuing external financing, leadership teams should examine how effectively their operations generate and retain cash. Improving collections, managing inventory and reinvesting profits can fund expansion without increasing debt or diluting ownership. Many companies leverage a portion of self-financing as a larger part of their capitalization strategy, even a small portion included in a larger debt or equity stake.

In a recent development, mailchimp demonstrated the potential of this approach, growing without outside equity financing before its acquisition by Intuit in a transaction valued at approximately $12 billion in 2021. Famously, Mailchimp avoided venture capital by prioritizing cash flow and streamlining operations to avoid needing outside capital. In 2020 and 2021, Mailchimp was pushing roughly $300 million in EBITDA.

Industry observers note that self-financing, however, is not equally practical across all industries. A software company with recurring revenue and modest infrastructure requirements has a different capital demand than a manufacturer purchasing machinery or a transportation company expanding its fleet. For asset-heavy businesses, relying exclusively on internal cash may constrain growth and allow competitors to capture emerging opportunities.

The goal is to maximize internal funding while preserving sufficient liquidity to withstand unexpected expenses, delayed payments and economic uncertainty.

Debt and equity represent fundamentally different approaches to financing expansion. Debt creates contractual repayment obligations, while equity exchanges ownership for capital without conventional repayment requirements. Neither approach is better than the other, across the board. Their suitability as financing options depends on the predictability of cash flows, the risks associated with expansion and the firm’s long-term objectives.

According to recent reports, in equipment finance, financing income-producing assets requires balancing borrowing costs, repayment schedules and anticipated returns. Credit decisions are partially based on these business fundamentals. The same principle applies to businesses investing in production equipment, facilities and other revenue-generating assets. When cash flows are predictable, borrowing can allow owners to retain equity while capturing the financial benefits of expansion. Companies should also recognize that repayment obligations remain even when growth underperforms, potentially restricting liquidity and operational flexibility.

Industry observers note that equity offers an alternative approach for companies developing upcoming technologies, entering uncertain markets or pursuing investments with unpredictable near-term returns. Investors share financial risk and may contribute valuable expertise and connections, but their capital comes at the expense of future ownership and profits. A founder selling 20% of a business may obtain the financing needed to accelerate growth while trading a portion of eventual value.

Investors may also negotiate governance rights, just as lenders may impose financial covenants, something I have considerable experience with in my role as a CFO. Consequently, the true cost of capital extends beyond interest rates and valuation to include the strategic flexibility a company retains. Sometimes, a captive business interest by an individual or institution through equity can supercharge a business through ongoing partnership.

Whether a business is considering relying on cash flow for growth, debt financing or trading equity for capital, the business should consider how much capital the firm needs and on what timeline.

An established distributor with predictable demand may use a revolving credit line to finance inventory and receivables, while a company developing an innovative product may require equity to support years of research and market development, like in the biotech industry. In fact, biotech companies can require several years of clinical trial stage development, requiring massive cash runways prior to even conceiving going to market; many of these companies involve acquisitions or exits at maturity.

Many businesses benefit from combining financing sources, using retained earnings for operational improvements, borrowing for established revenue-generating activities and reserving equity for investments involving greater uncertainty.

According to recent reports, capital structures should support corporate strategy rather than dictate it. Businesses should recognize the challenges of dilution and not seek to raise too much capital. The objective is to fund what needs to be funded. The financing strategy that allows the company to pursue growth, withstand setbacks and preserve its ability to create long-term value is the ideal approach for a company making a decision about financing growth.

Recent findings suggest that growth can create a real challenge for business leaders. The more successful a manufacturer becomes, the more capital it may require to keep growing and maintain or build on that level of success. Upcoming customers demand inventory; additional capacity requires equipment; product innovation and expansion into new markets often involve substantial investment before new revenue is realized.

In my role in senior financial leadership, I’ve learned that financing decisions involve both accessing capital and thoughtful strategy. These decisions shape a tech giant’s financial obligations, ownership structure and ability to pursue future opportunities. These decisions also shape the operating model of the company and the future trajectory of the business.

The challenge for companies experiencing growth is determining which combination of internal cash, debt and equity best supports the organization’s long-term ambitions. Any decision about capital strategy incorporates tradeoffs.

#684. How to protect your retirement savings if the AI bubble bursts

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 18m • 📚 Deep Dive (3622 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fastcompany ↗ Open Full Page

How to protect your retirement savings if the AI bubble bursts

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After stock markets, including the tech-heavy NASDAQ, got pummeled on Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that after stock markets, including the tech-heavy NASDAQ, got pummeled on Nov.
  • While markets rebounded the following Monday, this question still has profound implications for retirement savings, given how much these investment accounts are tied to stocks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After stock markets, including the tech-heavy NASDAQ, got pummeled on Nov. 20, 2026, many Americans are asking themselves whether the huge bet on artificial intelligence is heading south. While markets rebounded the following Monday, this question still has profound implications for retirement savings, given how much these investment accounts are tied to stocks. Before Monday’s surge, the NASDAQ had plunged about 18% since early October and had lost more than US$4 trillion since Nov. 16. The broad-based S&P 500 also took a beating and had shed all its gains for the year. As a finance professor and certified financial planner, I can’t tell you whether the bubble has truly burst for good. But I can explain how the default model that most 401(k) intends use works, where it protects you, and what you might consider changing. Whether AI stocks recover or not, the steps that protect a retirement account are the same: Know what you own, keep the mix of assets in balance, and hold enough in savings and low-risk funds to cover the years when you’ll need it. Here are some basic facts to guide your planning. Many Americans are saving on autopilot Most 401(k) savers hold a target-date fund, which is named for the year of your “target” retirement and is often chosen as a default option by the employer. To understand how the current stock market volatility affects retirement savings, it’s important to first explain how these funds work. About 55% of U.S. families have a defined contribution retirement account, such as a 401(k) or an individual retirement account. And inside a 401(k), the investing is increasingly done for you. Six in 10 plans administered by the fund giant Vanguard signed workers up automatically in 2025 when they started a latest job. And when those plans set a default investment, 98% of savers choose a target-date fund. About 60% of the nearly 5 million savers in those plans held a single target-date fund and nothing else. Taken together, target-date funds now hold $4.8 trillion. Inside each target-date fund is a list of index funds, which are named so because they track a particular market index. Vanguard’s series, the largest, is built mainly from four indices: U.S. stocks, international stocks, U.S. bonds and international bonds. The mix changes the older the saver gets, gradually moving away from high-return, high-risk stocks to safer, lower-yielding bonds. For example, Vanguard’s 2055 fund was just over 91% stocks at the end of September 2026, reflecting the relative youth of those holding it. That share drops to 16% for savers invested in the 2027 fund, who expect to retire imminently. Tech volatility is forcing new questions That autopilot model is now being tested, starting with Nvidia. In the span of a week, Nvidia went from riding the AI boom to getting mired in crisis. On Nov. 5, after the U.S. midterm elections raised the prospect of new curbs on AI and data centers, Nvidia shares fell more than 9%, while the broad-based S&P 500 index lost 4.4%. Then, on Nov. 12, Nvidia unveiled that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. By the end of that week, Nvidia had lost more than $1 trillion in market value within a month. That slide may now be reversed. Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang on Nov. 23, causing its share price to soar. More broadly, it’s too early to say whether the AI bubble is over. Some analysts argue that it’s just losing some air rather than bursting. But amid the turmoil in tech stocks, savers may wonder whether a retirement plan on autopilot should adjust to this fresh volatility. Target-date funds have significant tech exposure Target-date funds are marketed as broadly diversified, often holding thousands of stocks, and financial advisers repeated that point after Huang’s exit. But those stocks aren’t held in equal amounts. Index funds weight companies by market value. So as the value of AI-linked companies soared, their share has grown in the funds most 401(k) savers hold. And that gets to the question of whether there’s a tech bubble riding on overvalued AI companies. By the end of 2025, the 10 largest companies made up nearly 41% of the S&P 500, according to RBC Wealth Management. Yet those 10, almost all of which are in tech and AI, were expected to produce only about 32% of the index’s 2025 earnings. In other words, investors are paying a premium for these shares because they’re expecting great profits later. Bad news can shrink that premium quickly. Savers should also know that a target-date fund dilutes the concentration of AI stocks, but it doesn’t remove them. At the end of September, the 10 largest companies made up 36% of Vanguard’s total U.S. stock fund, with Nvidia at 7%. A 2055 fund keeps about 55% of its money there. So roughly 20 cents of every dollar was riding on 10 companies, and about 4 cents on Nvidia. That means even a small drop in these stocks can have a big impact on your fund, depending on its asset mix. And while diversification hedges against one organization’s turmoil, it’s less helpful if there’s a broad repricing of tech stocks. Even in Vanguard’s international fund, the four largest holdings are all tied to chipmaking, led by Taiwan Semiconductor, which makes Nvidia’s chips. Furthermore, diversification doesn’t mean guaranteed protection all the time. In 2008, during the global financial crisis, funds built for people retiring in 2010 lost nearly 24% on average. What to check now if you own a target-date fund In principle, savers don’t need to do anything as long as they choose to stay on autopilot until retirement. Fund managers buy and sell assets to stick to the target mix – a practice known as rebalancing. But rebalancing resets only the broad categories rather than trimming one particular company for growing too large. As Nvidia’s share of the market rose, so did its share of the fund. For people who hold just one target-date fund, I believe the right response to this month’s news is to leave their 401(k) account alone. The fund has been rebalancing all along, and your stake in any one company is modest. But a saver still needs to check three things. First, consider the year you expect to retire. If you want to move it earlier or later, or want more or less risk, you should choose a fund with a different year. Second, look at what the fund’s share of stocks is today, which is on the fund’s fact sheet. If you’re 60 and your fund is 60% stocks, a 30% fall in stocks would cut your balance by roughly 18%. If that would derail your retirement plans, you can switch to an earlier-dated fund that holds less in stocks and brings less risk. Third, if you have other funds, you should review them. About 1 in 4 target-date investors in Vanguard plans hold other funds. If you add a tech fund or an S&P 500 fund, your account is riskier and more concentrated than the label suggests. What to do if you hold other funds About 31% of savers in Vanguard plans opt out of target-date funds and choose their own investments, perhaps because they find target-date funds too conservative or their fees too costly. For these investors, and for anyone with old 401(k)s and IRAs, there is more to do. Start by looking at the fact sheet for each fund, like this one for Vanguard’s S&P 500 index fund, and compare the top holdings. An S&P 500 index fund, a large-cap growth fund and a technology or Nasdaq-tracking fund look like three investments. But in fact you may own the same handful of companies three times. Next, you should rebalance your holdings according to your plan, not to a prediction. That means returning to the mix of stocks and bonds that you chose in the first place. Trades inside a 401(k) don’t trigger taxes, and many plans offer automatic rebalancing. If yours doesn’t, a simple rule backed by Vanguard research works: review once or twice a year, and rebalance whenever any part of your mix drifts more than about 5 percentage points from your target. Finally, consider broadening the stocks you own. Morningstar Indexes strategist Dan Lefkovitz has pointed to U.S. value stocks, smaller companies and international stocks as areas with less AI exposure. Your plan may offer funds for each. None of these makes you immune to losses, and diversifying can mean trailing the hottest part of the market for years. But the pattern can flip quickly: International stocks gained about 29% in 2025, far ahead of the S&P 500’s 16%. Align your savings to your timeline How much this month’s news matters depends on when you’ll need the money. If you’re decades from retirement, a downturn can work in your favor, because every paycheck contribution buys shares at lower prices. Keep contributing and capture your full employer match. My own research with a colleague has found that accounts on systematic investment plans akin to 401(k)s earned better market-adjusted returns than accounts funded with lump sums. If you’re within 5-10 years of retirement, the bigger danger is what planners call sequence-of-returns risk: A large loss right before or just after you start withdrawing can permanently shrink what your savings can support. A good defense is to hold several years of expected withdrawals in lower-risk assets, such as bonds or money market funds, so you’re never forced to sell stocks after a drop. For retirees, Morningstar’s Christine Benz suggests one to two years of withdrawals in cash and five to eight more in bonds. What not to do The costliest mistake is usually the most tempting: selling everything and waiting for the dust to settle. During the 2008-09 financial crisis, about 117,000 Fidelity 401(k) participants moved entirely out of stocks. Those who stayed out saw their balances grow just 2% by mid-2011, while those who kept some stock exposure saw balances rise 50% on average. Other moves to avoid include stopping your own 401(k) contributions, chasing whatever theme looks safe this month, and pulling money out early, which can mean taxes, penalties and a locked-in loss. Last, don’t hand the decision to a chatbot. It will likely give you sound general guidance, such as diversifying and not panic-selling, and that consensus advice is where AI is reliable. But it is weakest on high-stakes questions that turn on your own situation. This story was updated on Nov. 23, 2006, to note Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as Nvidia’s CEO and the rebound in the company’s share price. Latest Update: Black Friday 2026: These unexpected items are driving up U.S. consumer spending

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1651 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
