💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the U.S.
  • retail industry’s version of the Super Bowl is here with the arrival of Black Friday, an occasion that sellers online and in stores seize to drive year-end sales.
  • Industry observers note that this year’s holiday shopping takes place in a U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the U.S. retail industry’s version of the Super Bowl is here with the arrival of Black Friday, an occasion that sellers online and in stores seize to drive year-end sales. This year, the day once considered the holiday shopping season’s unofficial kickoff might look to spectators more like the fourth quarter of a football game.Brands and retailers have promoted steep discounts under the Black Friday banner all month, and some began rolling out deals before Halloween. But enough die-hard traditionalists hit the shops as soon as they can after Thanksgiving that the day remains the year’s biggest for foot traffic at physical stores, according to Sensormatic Solutions, a retail technology company.“Black Friday is still the day for in-store shopping,” said Grant Gustafson, Sensormatic’s head of retail consulting and analytics.Stores also have kept drawing a majority of holiday season spending, although e-commerce captures a bigger share every year, according to U.S. Census data. Industry analysts expect the trend to continue; consumers spent $82.5 billion online from November 1 to November 22, a 9.1% increase from the comparable three weeks last year, according to research by Adobe.Retailers and consumers are giving Black Friday 2026 some other twists. The day’s evolution into a multiweek event has encouraged shoppers to stock up on discounted household basics while checking off their holiday lists, retail analysts said. Artificial intelligence and cost concerns are influencing how, where, when and on what consumers spend, retail analysts said.“It’s not just a moment where shoppers are buying gifts,” said Caila Schwartz, a retail and consumer insights leader at Salesforce. “They’re also buying things that they need, and so that’s going to help drive up a lot of the spend.”Here’s more on the emerging trends for Black Friday and holiday shopping overall: Low views of the economy aren’t expected to dim holiday sales This year’s holiday shopping takes place in a U.S. economic environment marked by voter frustration over gasoline prices fueled by the U.S. war with Iran, and high inflation overall.Analysts and economists scrutinize retail spending on the five days that begin with Thanksgiving Day and end on Cyber Monday for clues about consumers’ financial staying power and commercial prospects heading into the new year.Retail sales were up and down all year as filling up a car and other nonnegotiable costs took more out of household budgets. Commerce Department figures for October revealed Americans pulling back on buying books, clothes, sporting goods, and other items.The good news for retailers is that consumer confidence jumped this month as U.S. gas prices continued a steady decline.The National Retail Federation estimated that higher prices would account for about half of the 4.1% sales growth it expected in stores and online in November and December. The group forecast U.S. shoppers collectively spending $1.01 trillion. Black Friday still might have bigger discounts despite early deals U.S. retailers have broadly held the line on prices instead of making major increases across the board, and offered solid discounts that persuaded customers to shop earlier, industry analysts said.Salesforce, which tracks digital spending at a range of retailers, including grocery stores, said November discounts before Black Friday were 8% bigger than last year’s. Early promotions pushed average selling prices of physical merchandise 1% below last November’s prices, Salesforce said.Retailers nonetheless were likely to reserve their best prices for Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday, Vivek Pandya, director of digital insights at Adobe, said.For example, discounts on TVs are expected to average 23% on Friday compared with 11% during the first 22 days of the month, according to Adobe. Shoppers are buying household items along with holiday gifts The deepest discounts between this past Tuesday and Monday were expected on clothing, home goods, and health and beauty, Salesforce said. The company said it expected health and beauty products to average 33% off.With Black Friday commencing well before the day itself, some consumers apply seasonal bargains to last long after the holidays by filling their cupboards with toiletries and clothes they would typically buy at another time, according to analysts.Online sales of personal hygiene products were 40% higher from November 1 through November 22 compared with the October average, according to Adobe’s data. Sales of household cleaning products spiked 33% and clothing basics by 27% during the same time frame, Adobe said.“Usually, when you think of holiday shopping, it’s premium handbags and jewelry and those types of items, but we’re fast seeing shoppers also use this season to stock up on the essentials,” Pandya said. AI tools may be persuading users to do more online shopping Consumers are using AI-powered shopping tools to help them compare products and prices, particularly as inflation and paying more for gasoline have made them more attuned to price tags, Pandya said.Traffic to online retail sites from links in AI-powered tools more than doubled this month compared with November 2025, Adobe said.A belief that e-commerce sites will offer “the best value possible” has contributed to shoppers’ doing more of their holiday period spending online instead of in stores, Pandya said. —Anne D’Innocenzio, AP Retail Writer.

#680. 11 Gifts To Buy For The GTA 6 Fan In Your Life

11 Gifts To Buy For The GTA 6 Fan In Your Life

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Kotaku

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Kotaku)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As we approach the holiday season, we also approach the time when we all need to start buying gifts for people we know.
  • Here are 11 gift ideas for the GTA 6 fan in your life.
  • Assuming the GTA 6 fan in your life is playing on PS5 which, statistically speaking, is very likely, this is a fantastic option for them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As we approach the holiday season, we also approach the time when we all need to start buying gifts for people we know. Sometimes this can be annoying, but this year, if you have someone in your life who’s playing a ton of Grand Theft Auto 6 (and considering how many copies it’s sold, there’s a good chance you do!), there are some really easy gifts you can get them that will make them almost as happy as hanging out with Jason and Lucia.

Here are 11 gift ideas for the GTA 6 fan in your life. Just remember to figure out which console they’re playing on so you don’t get the wrong version of some of these gifts.

Assuming the GTA 6 fan in your life is playing on PS5 which, statistically speaking, is very likely, this is a fantastic option for them. Any version of this controller looks great and will let them explore Vice City in style.

Xbox doesn’t have an official GTA 6 controller, but you can find a really nice pink controller on sites like Amazon and Walmart. Just make sure you’re buying an officially branded Xbox controller and not some cheap knock-off that won’t feel good to use and will likely break after a few weeks. I’ve heard good things about this PowerA Vice City-inspired controller, but it uses a dongle or wire to connect, so keep that in mind.

Rockstar sells a variety of Grand Theft Auto 6 merch, like shirts and hats, on its official online store. If you aren’t sure what to get, I’ve got some of this stuff already, and I can easily recommend the tote bags. They’re well made, look cool, and are big enough to actually be useful while out and about. The shirts are also well made, but sizing runs small, so keep that in mind.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has some incredible music in it, and many of the game’s tracks were created just for GTA 6, includingÂ the banger opening song “Starting From Zero.” Any GTA 6 fan is going to be listening to these songs on repeat for some time, so why not buy them a nice version of the album? Sure, you can listen to it digitally, but for the real GTA 6 fans out there, owning a physical copy of the album will be a treat. And if they’re into vinyl, you can buy them this awesome-looking version of the GTA 6 album.

Speaking of physical copies of the game, perhaps buy them a boxed copy of GTA 6. It’s true, it doesn’t come with a disc, but if they bought the game digitally, they don’t have a physical object to hold onto. They also don’t have a cool paper map, either. And if you want, you can just take the code from inside; they don’t need it, so you can keep it for yourself if you’ve yet to buy GTA 6.Â.

Sources indicate that they might already have the game, but they might not have purchased the $100 version of GTA 6. So figure that out, and if they haven’t, buy them a $20 PSN or Xbox card so they can upgrade to the Ultimate Edition and check out all the extra cosmetic goodies available in-game.

Recent findings suggest that admittedly, this isn’t the best way to play the original Vice City. But it is a very easy way to play the original Vice City. And the GTA 6 fans in your life might be craving a trip to the original Vice City right now. With the Definitive Edition, which includes GTA 3, Vice City, and San Andreas, they can easily play the older games on the console and TV that they play GTA 6 on already. So while these remakes weren’t perfect, they’re convenient and can be bought physically, so you can wrap them up and pop them under the tree.

After playing a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6, I wanted to re-watch some classic crime movies. And at the top of my list were two all-timers set in Miami: Scarface and 2006’s Miami Vice.Â These can be found on Blu-ray pretty easily. If the GTA 6 fan in your life owns a PS5 or Xbox Series X console with a disc drive, you can buy them the 4K UHD version of Scarface. And next month, Miami Vice finally gets a director’s cut 4KUHD release. Perfect timing.

Recent findings suggest that yeah, sure, it’s not a GTA game, but Watch Dogs 2 is the closest Ubisoft ever got to matching the level of detail and fun found in actual Grand Theft Auto games. Plus, the game’s storyline about tech companies going too far and hackers fighting themselves and each other feels more relevant in 2026 than ever before.

According to recent reports, if the GTA fan in your life loved the grounded storytelling and realistic characters of GTA 6, then I’d recommend buying them Mafia: The Old Country on their platform of choice as a gift. Mafia: The Old Country is a shorter game than GTA 6, but it offers up some truly impressive visuals and a solid story about the old mafia in Italy and how dangerous, but alluring, it could be to those wanting a better life.

It has been revealed that hey, I own a few of these, and I love them so much. And after playing GTA 6, I’ve been busting them out of my closet when going to the store. So why not support your GTA 6 fan’s desire to live in Vice City and buy them a nice Hawaiian shirt? You can even find places selling knock-offs of Tommy Vercetti’s iconic blue Hawaiian shirt if you look around.

In a recent development, this is a gift that only works if they own a PS2 or a PS3 that can play PS2 games. But if they do, then maybe pick them up a copy of Vice City Stories on PS2. This is a somewhat rare GTA in 2026, as Rockstar never ported it to any other platforms after it launched on PSP, so outside of emulation and some in-development fan PC ports, the only way to play VCS is on a PS2. The game is also a bit hard to find these days, so just owning a copy of it is pretty cool. A lot of GTA fans have never played this game and might have forgotten about it at this point. This will get you plenty of cool points on Christmas.

#678. ‘It was the talk of the playground’: Google’s AI features blocked by L.A. school officials

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2366 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fastcompany ↗ Open Full Page

‘It was the talk of the playground’: Google’s AI features blocked by L.A. school officials

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2366 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that school districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the company gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices.
  • School districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the company gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices.
  • Industry observers note that schools are seeing growing backlash against technology, starting with cell phones and screen time and now focusing on AI, amid concerns that students are using AI to think for them.The Mountain View, California-based organization in August found itself at the center of controversy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that school districts are taking steps to block Google’s artificial intelligence features and are considering dropping Google products entirely unless the company gives them a permanent AI workaround, pitting them against the tech giant whose Chromebook computers and learning tools are deeply embedded in America’s classrooms.In a major step, Los Angeles school officials have quietly disabled AI-generated summaries, known as AI Overview, in Google searches on school-issued devices. The move makes the Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) the largest district to sideline the company, which has stated it will not separate its search product from AI tools for education.The L.A. district, which enrolls half a million students, has made no formal announcement, and the move caught parents and students by surprise, said Bridie Lee, a leader of Schools Beyond Screens LA, which has pushed for screen-time limits and tech oversight in the district.The group had several members who weighed in at a meeting of the Los Angeles school board’s AI committee on Friday, November 13. By that Monday, AI Overview was gone.“It was the talk of the playground,” Lee said.Google is the dominant provider of education technology for America’s classrooms. Beyond its low-cost Chromebooks, the most widely used student laptops, Google’s suite of education apps like Google Docs and Classroom has become integral to classwork, homework, and communication among students and teachers.But concerns about AI’s impact on learning have ignited a battle between schools and Google. In September, the country’s two largest school districts—in Newly introduced York and L.A.—declared one-year moratoriums on student use of generative AI, and Google has said it’s not possible to take AI out of its search products. Schools are considering other internet search providers.LAUSD said in a statement it temporarily suspended AI Overview to ensure student experiences are “age-appropriate and safe.” It also said it continually evaluates its digital safeguards, including third-party tools. It was likely using such a tool that it was able to disable AI Overview.Schools Beyond Screens LA asked parents to send videos of what laptop screens looked like and received clips showing that AI Overview was no longer an option in Google search on district devices. Then activists reached out to the district, which confirmed AI Overview was disabled. Lee said they had no other details on how it was done or how long it is intended to stay disabled.“We’re thrilled LAUSD did this,” said Lee. “AI is seeping into everything. It’s dangerous. It’s hurting learning. And it’s a corporate overreach into public schools. It’s Big Tech attempting to strongarm tech policy without anyone’s consent.”Other districts, such as Fairfax County Public Schools in Virginia, have developed plug-ins to remove AI summaries for students searching on Google, according to multiple published reports. Google is increasingly at center of school tech backlash Schools are seeing growing backlash against technology, starting with cell phones and screen time and now focusing on AI, amid concerns that students are using AI to think for them.The Mountain View, California-based company in August found itself at the center of controversy. That’s when it said it had turned on its Gemini chatbot for many K-12 students using Google Classroom, its learning management system. Weeks later, New York City and L.A. schools banned generative AI. In New York, the ban applies to all elementary and middle school students, and in Los Angeles all students K-12 are banned from using AI on school devices. Both districts said the ban would allow officials to develop AI policies this academic year.Then, in early November, Google backtracked. It published a blog post saying it would instead turn off Gemini and all search tools by default for K-12 schools in the coming months. Administrators would have to turn on each tool if they wanted students to access them.Google said this was to give schools more choice. But the choice to turn off AI altogether is not there.While the blog post does not explicitly say search can’t be used without AI, Chris Phillips, vice president for education at Google, told The New York Times: “Search and AI are deeply integrated.” If schools ban AI, students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.”The integration of AI in search isn’t new. Google introduced AI Overview in 2025, and anyone who uses Google search will get AI answers to many search results. Google insists AI Overview is an integral part of its search product now and cannot be separated.Earlier this month, hundreds of Google employees signed a petition asking the company’s leadership to allow schools to turn off AI features “without disrupting their ability to use search as a whole.”“The way the decision has been reported in the press is poor, and makes Google, and our Education and Search products as a result, look like we’re punishing schools for not using AI,” the petition said. “Many students, educators and parents have concerns about AI in the classroom, as is shown by many school districts who have placed moratoriums or bans on such technology. It is our job as Googlers to respect the user, and listen to them when they have concerns about our products.” Google has made some changes—but not enough, activists say Google notes it hears parents’ and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to “shortcut learning” and that it shares the same goal: helping students learn. But what many parents and teachers want—the ability to bypass AI entirely and allow students to use Google search like it was in, say, 2024—is not something Google offers. This has forced districts across the U.S. to choose between restricting students’ access to AI and maintaining access to the popular search engine.Instead of offering an AI-free search product for schools, Google announced a pilot “guided learning” tool that walks students “step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers.”“We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers,” the company said in a statement.Currently, Google search offers AI Overview, which contains summarized answers resulting from general searches, and AI Mode, which is a chatbot interaction. Guided learning, which is not yet available, will walk people through steps intended to support critical thinking to get to the answer.L.A. schools had already disabled Google’s AI Mode at the beginning of the school year on school-issued student devices, said Jack Kelanic, the district’s chief information officer, during a school board committee meeting on artificial intelligence last week. Educators and staff still have access.“We understand this as a deeper embedding of AI into the education suite,” Kelanic said. He added, to applause, that the district is not bound to Google’s products if officials determine the changes are not in line with the district’s priorities.“We have choices,” Kelanic said. “We can change the default search engine literally overnight.” The Associated Press’ education coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations. AP is solely responsible for all content. Find AP’s standards for working with philanthropies, a list of supporters and funded coverage areas at AP.org. —Barbara Ortutay, Jocelyn Gecker and Cheyanne Mumphrey, Associated Press.

Google insists AI Overview is an integral part of its search product now and cannot be separated.Earlier this month, hundreds of Google employees signed a petition asking the company’s leadership to allow schools to turn off AI features “without disrupting their ability to use search as a whole.”“The way the decision has been reported in the press is poor, and makes Google, and our Education and Search products as a result, look like we’re punishing schools for not using AI,” the petition said. “Many students, educators and parents have concerns about AI in the classroom, as is shown by many school districts who have placed moratoriums or bans on such technology. It is our job as Googlers to respect the user, and listen to them when they have concerns about our products.”.

In a recent development, google claims it hears parents’ and teachers’ concerns about students using AI to “shortcut learning” and that it shares the same goal: helping students learn. But what many parents and teachers want—the ability to bypass AI entirely and allow students to use Google search like it was in, say, 2024—is not something Google offers. This has forced districts across the U.S. to choose between restricting students’ access to AI and maintaining access to the popular search engine.Instead of offering an AI-free search product for schools, Google revealed a pilot “guided learning” tool that walks students “step-by-step through a range of complex problems, instead of just giving quick answers.”“We are actively building these experiences in partnership with educators, listening closely to ensure our products support students and teachers,” the firm noted in a statement.Presently, Google search offers AI Overview, which contains summarized answers resulting from general searches, and AI Mode, which is a chatbot interaction. Guided learning, which is not yet available, will walk users through steps intended to support critical thinking to get to the answer.L.A. schools had already disabled Google’s AI Mode at the beginning of the school year on school-issued student devices, said Jack Kelanic, the district’s chief information officer, during a school board committee meeting on artificial intelligence last week. Educators and staff still have access.“We understand this as a deeper embedding of AI into the education suite,” Kelanic said. He added, to applause, that the district is not bound to Google’s products if officials determine the changes are not in line with the district’s priorities.“We have choices,” Kelanic said. “We can change the default search engine literally overnight.”.

Sources indicate that the Associated Press’ education coverage receives financial support from multiple private foundations. AP is solely responsible for all content. Find AP’s standards for working with philanthropies, a list of supporters and funded coverage areas at AP.org.

—Barbara Ortutay, Jocelyn Gecker and Cheyanne Mumphrey, Associated Press.

Travis and Jason Kelce’s Garage Beer lands $20 million as craft brewers pull back

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1663 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew.
  • Industry observers note that travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew.
  • The funding comes at a time when the independent beer industry has been facing many challenges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Travis Kelce’s beer brand just secured a huge financial deal to help promote its popular brew. On Tuesday, Travis and his brother Jason Kelce’s Garage Beer brand secured a $20 million revolving credit from Tiger Finance, according to a release. The funding comes at a time when the independent beer industry has been facing many challenges. The rise in operation costs, slowing business openings, and declines in sales have forced many breweries to close down or refinance. But this celebrity-backed brand is only seeing success. Andy Cerussi, the senior managing director of Tiger Finance, noted in the release that the manufacturer is thrilled to have been chosen as the preferred financial partner, saying that the company is “impressed with [the] impact the Kelce brothers have had on positively influencing brand awareness.” Brian Amicon, president of Garage Beer, told Inc. that as the company continues to grow, this financing allows it greater flexibility. “From strengthening our distribution to investing in the brand and creating more opportunities to connect with consumers, it puts us in a strong position to keep building what we’ve started,” Amicon said. “We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and excited to keep pushing forward.” A $20 million bet on Garage Beer’s brand strength The debt deal allows Garage Beer to expand its product line and enter fresh markets. At $20 million, the financing sits on the smaller side of the funding spectrum—in the bottom quarter of deals tracked, according to Deal Room. But for a consumer company like a beer line, debt against brand strength gives growth capital without diluting equity. This revolving line will give Garage Beer flexible access to capital tied to its brand value. The Columbus, Ohio-based brand originally rolled out as a local craft light lager by Braxton Brewing Co., but was spun off into an independent company in 2023 by its CEO, Andy Sauer. According to VinePair, the Kelce brothers joined Garage Beer in the summer of 2024 by acquiring a majority stake and becoming co-owners and operators. This move rapidly boosted the brand’s national visibility. In late 2025, Durational Capital Management unveiled its strategic investment partnership with the company. A cofounder of Durational Capital said in the release that the company appreciates Tiger’s creativity and partnership “to structure a credit facility that leverages the strength of Garage Beer’s brand to support the company’s growth objectives.” Garage Beer is expanding while competitors retrench Neil Reid, a professor at the University of Toledo who studies the craft beer industry, told Inc. that the brand’s trajectory stands out. “Garage Beer’s aggressive expansion is highly unusual in today’s beer market,” Reid said. He noted that the company has expanded distribution to all 50 states and added more than 100,000 barrels of volume in 2025, reportedly the largest increase among U.S. craft brewers. “Rather than retrenching, Garage Beer is using the downturn to gain market share from competitors,” Reid told Inc. He added that brands with the capacity for growth through distribution often tend to be a simple product and have broad appeal, sales momentum, enough capital to fund expansion, name recognition, and scalable operations. Brands like small craft breweries that rely on taprooms and direct sales struggle with reaching that same momentum. Even if they have strong local followings, having fewer financial resources and less distributor support can be a challenge. “By offering a simple, familiar product rather than a niche craft beer, the brand can attract a larger audience, generate stronger retail turnover, and expand more easily across geographic markets,” Reid said. But he cautioned against treating Garage Beer as a model for the rest of the industry, noting, “The brand benefits from factors that most breweries lack, including celebrity backing, substantial capital, extensive marketing reach, and a highly scalable business model. Differentiation remains important, but differentiation alone is rarely sufficient.” Celebrity attention still has to translate into repeat sales Claudia Kubowicz Malhotra, marketing professor at the University of North Carolina’s Kenan-Flagler Business School, told Inc. that celebrity attention is only the first step. “To continue to build the brand, awareness needs to translate to interest, desire, and action,” Kubowicz Malhotra said. “Consumers need to look and ask for the beer by name. Ultimately, this needs to translate to sales.” As Garage Beer adds new products, she said, it can grow successfully “if new product offerings reinforce the brand positioning—a light beer that tastes like beer.” To judge whether the brand has staying power, Kubowicz Malhotra told Inc. she would look beyond sales: “I would also look for customer retention and repurchase behavior as well as word of mouth.” Tiger Finance and Durational Capital Management did not immediately respond to Inc.’s request for comment. —Lucia Auerbach This article originally appeared on Fast Company’s sister website, Inc.com. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NASA experiments, including a first-of-its-kind space crop production system, will travel to the International Space Station aboard Northrop Grumman’s 25th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency.

Investigations from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division will advance research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration, expanding knowledge of space crops and human health.

It has been revealed that astronauts will need sustainable sources of food to travel farther and stay longer in space. To help understand how crop production works in microgravity, NASA is launching a novel space crops experiment.

Industry observers note that the newly introduced prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing safe, nutritious, and reliable crop production systems for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Knowledge gained from the space crop production system also could help inform agricultural practices such as vertical farming and indoor growing systems.

Researchers will use this investigation to validate the system’s water delivery and volume optimization technology aboard the space station.

A precision health investigation is the next step toward enabling long-duration studies of human brain tissues in space.

It has been revealed that the research builds on a previous investigation that sent small, lab-grown models of the human brain, called miBrains, to the space station. This experiment will validate a miniature fluid-handling system designed to mix, deliver, and maintain the nutrient-rich liquid needed to keep the tissues alive.

Researchers could use the findings to help identify potential neurological risks associated with spaceflight and develop strategies to protect astronaut health. It also may advance human tissue research and neurological disease modeling on Earth.

Sources indicate that NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division pioneers scientific discovery and enables exploration by using space environments to conduct investigations not possible on Earth. Studying biological and physical phenomena under extreme conditions allows researchers to advance the fundamental scientific knowledge required to go farther and stay longer in space, while also benefitting life on Earth.

Southwest Airlines is offering 55 days of buy-one-get-one flights. Here’s how to get them

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year.
  • In a recent development, southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year.
  • On Friday, Southwest revealed a three-day promotion that allows Rapid Rewards members to earn a temporary Companion Pass by booking and completing just one round-trip flight or two one-way flights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southwest Airlines is taking a slightly different approach to Black Friday this year. Rather than simply discounting flights, the airline is giving travelers an opportunity to earn one of its most coveted perks: the Companion Pass. On Friday, Southwest announced a three-day promotion that allows Rapid Rewards members to earn a temporary Companion Pass by booking and completing just one round-trip flight or two one-way flights. The offer comes just weeks before Southwest is set to overhaul its Rapid Rewards loyalty program, significantly changing how travelers qualify for the benefit. How to earn Southwest’s promotional Companion Pass If you’re already planning to fly over the holidays, earning the pass could be relatively easy. To take advantage of the promotion, travelers will need to: Register for the promotion through Southwest. Book eligible flights between November 27 and November 29. Complete either a single round-trip flight or two one-way flights between November 27 and January 5, 2027. Travelers who score the pass will be able to bring a designated companion on eligible flights between January 8 and March 3, 2027 for free, with the exception of taxes and fees, which start at $5.60 each way. There’s also no limit to the number of eligible flights travelers can use the pass for during the promotional period, so you and your companion could, in theory, go on a 2-month adventure only paying for one of your flights. Southwest is changing how travelers earn a Companion Pass The promotion comes at an interesting time for Southwest. In October, the airline unveiled changes to its Rapid Rewards loyalty program that will take effect on January 1, 2027. Under the existing program, travelers can earn a Companion Pass by completing 100 qualifying one-way flights or accumulating 135,000 Companion Pass qualifying points in a calendar year. Starting in January, Southwest will eliminate Companion Pass qualifying points and instead use Tier Qualifying Points to determine eligibility for elite status and Companion Pass benefits. The airline is also introducing a latest milestone reward that gives members three Companion Pass trips, while travelers who reach its new Platinum elite status will receive unlimited companion trips. One of the biggest changes is how credit card rewards factor into the equation. Historically, Southwest credit card welcome bonuses have offered a particularly lucrative shortcut to earning a Companion Pass. Starting in 2027, those bonuses will no longer count toward qualification. The same goes for referral bonuses, anniversary points, and points earned through hotel and rental car partners. Everyday spending on Southwest credit cards will still help travelers qualify, with cardholders earning one Tier Qualifying Point per dollar spent. There’s still time to earn a Companion Pass under the old rules Southwest is giving prospective credit card customers one final opportunity to take advantage of the existing qualification structure. Travelers who apply for a Southwest Rapid Rewards credit card by December 14, are approved, and meet the spending requirements for its welcome bonus can still have those bonus points count toward earning a Companion Pass under the 2026 rules, even if they complete the spending requirement in early 2027. Those who meet the overall qualification requirements can enjoy unlimited companion flights through December 31, 2027. For travelers who don’t fly Southwest often enough to qualify for the traditional Companion Pass, however, this weekend’s Black Friday promotion offers a much easier way to experience the perk, even if only for a couple of months.

It has been revealed that the people at Sony don’t use words like “product” or “reboot” when they talk about Aibo, the Japanese electronics and entertainment company’s robotic dog.Aibo robots, which first went on sale in 1999, are all sold out and no longer in production. But some owners who had to part with their Aibo have donated the robots to Tokyo-based Sony Group Corp. for an “adoption program,” where they get treated to repairs and upgrades.Those robot pets now have new homes in hospitals and other facilities, bringing solace and smiles to patients and staff.Sony does not disclose the pricing or the number of Aibo robots that have been sold.Packed with sensors, digital cameras and an intelligence of sorts, Aibo has been programmed to remember its name, the owner’s face and its surroundings — details of everyday life that make for a disarming illusion of a personality.The robot barks, cocks its head, moves its ears, waddles toward you, acts happy when petted and goes to “sleep” — in short it simulates a puppy, except this one can take snapshots and monitors its own mechanical dysfunctions.“The owners feel as though they are sending off what has become to them like their own child,” noted Sony official Yoshiyuki Katsuno, who oversees the program.Aibo gets people talking to each other, and can offer tired souls a perk to pick themselves up and keep going, according to Katsuno.“We hope to spread the emotional healing and human interaction that Aibo has to offer,” he said.At the St. Marianna University School of Medicine in Kawasaki, on the outskirts of Tokyo, a nurse had to do some looking to find a wandering Aibo during a recent visit.But Aibo has helped with the long waits for visiting patients and succeeded in persuading reluctant children to get examined, indicates Dr. Manabu Komori of the department of otolaryngology.That field involves diagnosing and treating sicknesses related to the ear, nose and throat, with many child patients.“It helps motivate the kids,” Komori said. “Going to a hospital is basically not very pleasant.”The hospital also uses real dogs to help patients feel better, though the animals require care and food and can be temperamental. That means a robot dog offers some advantages, although Komori was careful not to say they were better than real dogs.Cuteness is seen as desirable in Japanese culture, where being “kawaii,” or “cute,” is not a sign of weakness or inferiority, but an endearing trait that encourages harmony and communication — both valued in Japanese society.And so, if the need is for a soulmate, it’s better to have that cute look, be it a dog, cat or even a duck, said Jerry Wang, Executive Chairman of FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem, a U.S. company that offers more foreboding-looking four-legged patrol robots.“If you want some emotional attachment, you want a cute shape,” he said. This gaming mouse should be a Logitech-killer, but it has one substantial flaw

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Keychron’s G6 HE uses magnetic switches like Logitech’s Superstrike mice, but the clicks are all off.﻿.

  • According to recent reports, if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Keychron’s G6 HE uses magnetic switches like Logitech’s Superstrike mice, but the clicks are all off.﻿.

Keychron’s G6 HE uses magnetic switches like Logitech’s Superstrike mice, but the clicks are all off.﻿.

According to recent reports, if you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Sources indicate that when Keychron declared its $90 G6 HE gaming mouse, I immediately thought, “Cool! A cheaper alternative to the pricey $180 Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike.” Logitech’s innovation with the Superstrike is using magnetic Hall effect switches for a user-adjustable mouse click depth, with haptic vibrations mimicking the tactile click feel. The Keychron G6 HE, as its name indicates, also uses Hall effect switches for that same kind of customization. But something felt immediately off as I began testing it.

The mouse’s shape and design are very reminiscent of Logitech G Pro models, with more colorful flair. The magnetic switches are there and easily customizable (through a browser-based app, no less). But the clicks? The clicks are all wrong.

Industry observers note that the left and right mouse buttons on the G6 HE use Keychron’s MagOptic switches, which are both magnetic Hall effect and optical. They click just like any standard mouse, regardless of where you set the actuation point. There are no fancy haptics on the Keychron. If you set the buttons to a shallow hair-trigger depth, you’ll register a press before you actually feel or hear any click. Set the depth for a very heavy press, and the mouse clicks before it actually registers. That… kind of defeats the purpose here.

According to recent reports, there’s not much point in tuning the actuation depth of the G6 HE’s buttons if the click feel doesn’t match it. I suppose it’s still nice to have a hair-trigger-like setting for taking faster single shots in an FPS, but not feeling anything when you shoot is weird. And it gets frustrating when using the G6 HE as a regular mouse for productivity — like you’re getting phantom clicks as you mouse around your computer. At least I can feel my accidental clicks when using a Logitech Superstrike with the action set too high, and I know I’m to blame for leaving the mouse on my try-hard settings.

Sources indicate that I reached out to Keychron for the reasoning behind the G6 HE’s magnetic-but-not-haptic setup, and cofounder Fab Chan mentioned, “There are two reasons for this design. First, many people still prefer the feel of a traditional click over haptics. Second, a haptic motor adds weight, and for this model we prioritized a lighter design. That said, we’re planning a model with haptic feedback. It will be slightly heavier than the G6 HE, and we’ll share more details soon.”.

The G6 HE is a lightweight mouse. It’s only 49g with its battery, or 40g in wired mode with the battery removed. The Logitech X2 Superstrike is 60g, and the newer X3 Superstrike is 59g — each still pretty light. If you ignore all the Hall effect stuff and just use the G6 HE as a regular mouse, it has some things going for it over the Superstrikes. In addition to its lighter build and much lower price, it feels a tiny bit comfier in my hand, thanks to its side walls that curve slightly inward at the bottom.

Recent findings suggest that one of its best features is hot-swappable batteries. From my time testing Angry Miao’s AM Infinity Mouse, I know that once you can pop out a magnetic battery pack and quickly swap it, you never want to go back to plugging in your mouse to charge. You can also get the G6 HE in black with a standard built-in rechargeable battery for $15 less, but I don’t think that’s enough savings to forgo the convenience of hot-swap batteries.

The G6 HE’s charging base doubles as the wireless receiver, and of course it’s lit up with customizable RGB lighting. It has four programmable buttons for on-the-fly changes to things like DPI, lighting, mouse profiles, or just about anything else you want to program. The browser-based Keychron Launcher software is robust and makes tinkering with the G6 HE or its base very easy. And for some reason, the receiver / charging base is designed like a vacuum tube, which is fun, but it means you’re unscrewing its clear housing to access the battery — a little tedious.

I can’t shake my disappointment with the G6 HE’s lackadaisical magnetic switch implementation. Keychron seems proud of the fancy MagOptic Switch it put into the G6 HE, even going so far as to call it “next gen,” but this mouse seems a jack of all trades and master of none. The G6 HE is cheaper than most other mice with hot-swap batteries — which can still make it worthwhile if you don’t care about all the Hall effect stuff — but that is its lone saving grace.

We’ll have to wait and see if Keychron’s follow-up model with haptics can properly compete with the Superstrike mice and their hallmark feature. I’m excited to see where Hall effect tech goes in mice, and how more companies can evolve it, but the G6 HE is a half-measure.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your kid is becoming quite the capitalist.
  • child with an active Trump account will soon receive two shares of SpaceX, the space exploration firm run by Elon Musk.
  • Recent findings suggest that spaceX confirmed Wednesday that the company will donate one share of its Class A common stock—currently trading for more than $130 per share—to every currently active Trump account.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your kid is becoming quite the capitalist. Every U.S. child with an active Trump account will soon receive two shares of SpaceX, the space exploration tech giant run by Elon Musk. This donation marks the latest in a string of philanthropic initiatives focused on these newly introduced types of tax-advantaged investment accounts. SpaceX unveiled Wednesday that the company will donate one share of its Class A common stock—right now trading for more than $130 per share—to every currently active Trump account. In turn, CEO Musk will match that donation, which he later confirmed on X. “Every child in America will receive two SpaceX shares, one from the company and one from me personally,” Musk posted. In its official announcement, SpaceX touted its future-focused mission of building new infrastructure that could achieve multiplanetary living. “We believe ownership of the company creating these systems should extend to the next generation of Americans for their long-term benefit.” Here’s what we know about the donations. MILLIONS OF NEW SHAREHOLDERS The portfolios of the country’s youngest generation of investors keep getting fatter. Introduced earlier this year, Trump accounts allow deposits of up to $5,000 per year for each child until the age of 18 and various billionaires have even thrown some money into the mix. Musk now joins the likes of Michael Dell and Ray Dalio, who have similarly pledged donations to Trump accounts. The U.S. Treasury Department, too, will make a one-time $1,000 deposit to every child born between Jan. 1, 2025, and Dec. 31, 2028. The SpaceX shares work a little differently in that the company will transfer one share of its stock to active Trump accounts in December, according to Musk’s post. Nearly 70 million accounts have been created thus far, the White House reported last month, though that’s largely a result of a change by the Treasury to allow for automatic enrollment. Musk’s matching donation will come later, he remarked on X, sometime after mid-June 2027. That’s when a 366-day lockup expires that he agreed to as part of the SpaceX initial public offering earlier this year. The Starbase, Texas-based company noted that Gwynne Shotwell, its president and chief operating officer, previously pledged with her husband to donate more than 2 million shares to Trump accounts. But there are strict eligibility requirements associated with those donations, which parents can check online. Combined, the gifts from the company, Musk, and Shotwell could have a value of more than $18 billion given the stock’s current price and if all eligible Trump accounts have been claimed. These donations also do something that’s delving into new territory: They guarantee that potentially millions of Americans will become long-term shareholders of SpaceX. YOU GET A STOCK! Just as Oprah famously announced a new car to every person in her studio audience back in the early 2000s, Musk and other billionaires are saying the same to kids now: “You get a stock!” But that could create a conundrum of sorts for parents as more and more money is likely to flow into these accounts from billionaires. The Treasury recently implemented new rules that allow companies and other donors to gift individual stocks to these accounts, while also limiting trading activity in them, as The Wall Street Journal reported. Children and their parents can neither pick nor reject stocks that are donated to a child’s account—and they can’t sell them for five years. And yet, there’s free money on the line. If parents don’t claim an account on behalf of their kid, their kid misses out on a potentially lucrative portfolio. Despite the move to automatic enrollment, some manual steps are still required, which means parents need to claim an account by downloading an app from the Trump accounts website. Musk couldn’t help but tout the prospects of what that could mean to millions of prospective shareholders—something that resonated with investors, too, as the stock has jumped nearly 5% in the past two days of trading. “If SpaceX succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy, it will be worth about a million times the current global economy,” Musk posted. “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them. I recommend holding on to your shares.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that DFor centuries archaeologists have attempted to learn the origins of what we believe was known as Bleak Friday. Theories have long-pointed toward some sort of national purge day, in which citizens of the United States were encouraged to murder one another in the pursuit of widescreen televisions. But more and more evidence is being unearthed that it might have been a day of mourning due to not knowing which indie game to play next. To prevent a repeat of such a tragic era of human history, we at Kotaku 3000 are introducing preventative measures, and have compiled together 12 completely excellent lesser-known indie games to keep the bleakness away.

Recent findings suggest that or indeed, I asked developers to email me about their recently released or upcoming games that aren’t getting any attention, so I could stick them on the front page of the site while the bosses are distracted by sales. 12 such games went up on the site yesterday, and here are 12 more! I really cannot get over the incredible variety, originality and excellence on display here. Some are already out and can be bought, and the rest deserve a place on your wishlist.

Developer: Pandan Games Release date: Q2 2027 Steam.

An indie game inspired byÂ Ratchet & Clank is a tall order, but it really looks like Pandan Games could do it.Â GearGrit is a third-person platformer where you play as Tansy Geargrit, escaping from prison for crimes she maybe only committed some of, and attempting to unearth a giant government conspiracy.

Developer: darqwerful Release date: TBA Steam.

Detective games are having such an excellent resurgence, andÂ The Detective’s Apprentice looks to be offering a deep, pure example of the form. You play as Cleo, the niece of famous detective Maya Lynch, searching for clues and making logical deductions to solve crimes and murders. Thematically it looks to be of an Agatha Christie era, with all sorts of crime reconstruction, interviewing, information gathering, and all that good stuff. There is a demo, although no release date yet.

Developer: Sebastian Gioseffi Release date: Out now Steam.

“A very short game about the very best part of video games: the menus,” reads the store description forÂ Video Game Menu: The Game. And boy, does it have a lot of menus. Menus with buttons! And toggles! And an option for “cursorphobic buttons.” There’s also an option for “looming figure” which seems a bit unsettling. And apparently a way to get a flight sim HUD. It looks wonderfully bonkers, and you can buy and play it right now.

Developer: Mothman Mothman Studios Release date: Out now Steam.

I suppose you could argue thatÂ PokÃ©mon Snap is a form of cryptid cam game, butÂ CryptidCam is the real thing. This super-cute game is about taking photos of sweet little woodland oddities, including the likes of the Loch Ness Monster, bigfoot, and the Loveland Frogman (my new obsession), as well as just gorgeous beasties with extra horns. You add your photos to the Cryptid-Nomicon, all for the sake of mysterious cryptozoologist Dr. Ted Krupp, and enough of my waffle, it’s out now so I’m already installing it.

Developer: Chaparral Collective, Unspeakable Pixels Release date: 2027 Steam.

It has been revealed that unspeakable Pixels made 2020’s utterly wonderfulÂ Batbarian: Testament of the Primordials, and you should definitely go buy and play that immediately. Do that while waiting for next year’sÂ Gift of the Primordials, a turn-based puzzle game about…balancing soil nutrients? No, come back, it looks really good! It’s about building habitats for fantasy wildlife through puzzle mechanics based around judicious placement of plants. I’m still not selling it well. Watch the trailer. And playÂ Batbarian.

Developer: Sunna Entertainment Release date: TBA Steam.

According to recent reports, surely this can’t be the first time someone’s thought to crossÂ Tetris with a platform game? But I’ve certainly never seen it before. And hot-damn, check out the animation work in the trailer above. This just looks phenomenal, with multiple characters and loadouts, buildingÂ Tetrisy towers in order to attack enemies, build combos and gather new skills. There’s a demo to check it out right now, but no sign of a release date yet.

Developer: Gabriel Maldonado Release date: Dec 4 Steam.

Sources indicate that “Flash is fragile,” notes the blurb forÂ Ad Iterum, “but you can hack it.” Eek. This top-down turn-based roguelike looks gloriously macabre, with wonderful pixel art, as you descend through dungeons mutating your own body through the devouring of your enemies. It’s about seeing how far down you dare go, before attempting to return to the surface with your ill-gotten gains, with unique combinations of mutations defining each run through the procedurally generated world. And it’s out next week!

Developer: Little Sister Games Release date: 2027 Steam.

Sources indicate that as we all know, the way through the underworld is not via well-timed combat, but through the rolling of dice.Â Lovers Die is a Yahtzee-inspired roguelite, rolling dice to eliminate categories as you build up attacks. I adore the art here, those crunchy pixels and the wonderful way descriptive text is presented. Also, why aren’t more dicebuilders based on Yahtzee?! This is a darker, more adult game that the art might initially suggest, and looks compelling. We have to wait until next year to play it.

Developer: Fe Angelo, 2dchaos Release date: TBA Steam, Itch.

Oh my goodness, you have to check out how this third-person survival horror uses color. It’s stunning. I mean, everything about the art is stunning.Â NechromiaÂ is about escaping a gothic castle built of someone else’s memories, with only a lantern to protect you. This looks so incredibly promising, and there’s a demo available on the Itch page for the game.

Developer: Dagada’s Team, Matthieu Lu Release date: TBA Steam.

Gosh, this immediately induced some nostalgia.Â Dagada’s Story looks deeply reminiscent of the Atari/Amiga era of 16-bit platformers, complete with a mascot-like main character. You play as Dagada and his flying chum Naou, able to control each separately in order to solve puzzles, with the goal of saving the harmony of an alien mountain in order to repair Dagada’s spaceship and get home. It looks very charming, and there’s already a demo to check out.

Developer: Stellar Cartography Interactive Release date: Out now Steam.

Is it OK to decide you already like a game entirely based on the pun in its title?Â Prophet MarginÂ is part city builder, part board game and part strategy, all about creating trade routes that please the gods. The emphasis is on calm, meditative play, with lots of deep thinking and methodical planning, as well as appeasing the deities of each resource. It came out just a few weeks ago, and for those who’ve discovered it is proving very well-received, although the unfortunate closure of the intended publisher means it’s not yet found enough eyes.

Developer: Goloso Games Release date: TBA Steam.

Sources indicate that one-person team Goloso Games made 2021’s excellentÂ Inspector Waffles, a great point-and-click adventure that is well worth your time. Their next game isÂ Antenna Dilemma, a new adventure featuring C432632, a grey cube who discovers there’s more to reality than his sofa and TV. It looks superbly bizarre, and there’s a demo out there already if you want to find out more.

A popular password manager was hacked. Here’s what you need to know

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (991 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security.
  • Password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security.
  • In a recent development, popular Password manager 1Password disclosed this week that hackers breached its systems this month and accessed the software’s source code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security. Popular Password manager 1Password disclosed this week that hackers breached its systems this month and accessed the software’s source code. While no breach is good news, the attackers were not able to access 1Password users’ most sensitive data, including their passwords, secret keys, and information stored in user vaults. “At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the manufacturer emphasized in a blog post on the incident. The security of the software maker’s apps and browser extensions was also not affected by the breach. The attackers were able to burrow into 1Password’s system after gaining access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. By pushing malicious code into its backend systems, the attackers made off with administrative data on a subset of 1Password customers, including customer names, email addresses, and “non-secret internal metadata” about accounts. Anyone who uses 1Password doesn’t need to take extra steps right now, but they should be extra vigilant for phishing attempts in the future. That includes being skeptical of “unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts,” according to the company. The password manager will never ask its customers for an account password or a secret key. In response, 1Password notes that it has disabled the compromised GitHub account, rotated and revoked exposed internal credentials, and brought in external cybersecurity experts to advise the software maker on its response, among other measures. Security for everybody The world of cybersecurity moves fast – and now that cycle is speeding up even in light of AI. Security companies are leveraging artificial intelligence to detect threats at the same time that malicious actors are putting it to work cracking into accounts at scale. 1Password CTO Nancy Wang described the unique challenges and opportunities the company faces in light of widespread AI adoption in a recent interview with Fast Company. While a sea of vibe-coded apps have introduced security holes human software makers would have caught, AI can also scan massive chunks of code for vulnerabilities. “AI’s been a mixed bag, just because that work has been so gnarly and technical,” Wang mentioned. Aside from the millions of people who rely on 1Password, more than 200,000 businesses use the password manager to keep track of their credentials. That number includes nearly a third of the largest companies in the U.S., according to 1Password. Fast Company named the software maker to its 2025 list of Brands That Matter for its user-friendly approach to security. “1Password was built on the belief that security should be accessible to everyone,” 1Password CEO David Faugno said last year. “In an industry that too often leads with fear and complexity, we’ve built our foundation on trust, usability, and the human experience.”.

Breaking: The 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade isn’t canceled. Here’s when you can watch it this weekend

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fastcompany

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
🎬 5-Second Live Source Screen Capture (Fastcompany)
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thanksgiving may be over, but one of the holiday’s biggest traditions is still to come.
  • Thanksgiving may be over, but one of the holiday’s biggest traditions is still to come.
  • Recent findings suggest that for the first time in its history, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is taking place on a day other than Thanksgiving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanksgiving may be over, but one of the holiday’s biggest traditions is still to come. For the first time in its history, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is taking place on a day other than Thanksgiving. On Wednesday, Macy’s, NBC, and New York City officials made the unprecedented decision to postpone the parade until Saturday, November 28, after forecasts called for dangerous winds, heavy rain, and coastal flooding. While the parade was canceled from 1942 through 1944 during World War II, weather has never before forced organizers to move the event to another day. The timing is particularly noteworthy given that this year marks the parade’s 100th edition, a milestone Macy’s is celebrating with an expanded lineup of balloons, floats, musical performances, and celebrity appearances. NBC aired a replay of the 2025 parade on Thanksgiving morning instead. The live celebration will take place Saturday, although the last-minute schedule change has forced some performers to adjust their looks. Here’s what to expect from the rescheduled parade and how to watch it. Who is performing at the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade? Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb, and Al Roker are slated to return as hosts of NBC’s broadcast. The originally announced musical lineup includes RAYE, Teddy Swims, Megan Moroney, Natasha Bedingfield, Queen Latifah, Jimmy Fallon and The Roots, JoJo, Smash Mouth, and Keke Palmer, among others. A special Broadway performance featuring a 10-minute medley from nine musicals, including Hamilton, Wicked, and Rent, is still expected to take place. The Radio City Rockettes are also on the announced lineup. However, not everyone who planned to participate on Thursday will be able to stick around for Saturday. The University of Alabama’s Million Dollar Band, for instance, is returning home to perform at Saturday’s Iron Bowl football game. Macy’s Great American Marching Band is also unable to participate in the rescheduled event. Other groups have turned to crowdfunding to cover the unexpected cost of extending their stays in New York. A high school marching band from Pearland, Texas, raised $350,000 in less than 24 hours to enable more than 500 students and staff members to stay for the parade. How to watch the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade The rescheduled parade will step off at 8:30 a.m. ET on Saturday, November 28, and is expected to conclude around noon. NBC will televise the parade, while cord-cutters can stream it on Peacock. A Spanish-language broadcast will also be available on Telemundo. Viewers with live TV streaming subscriptions that carry NBC, including YouTube TV, Hulu + Live TV, and Fubo, can also tune in. If you’d rather sleep in on Saturday morning, NBC is scheduled to air an encore presentation at 2 p.m. ET/PT.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • An analysis of protein-coding DNA from more than 1.4 million people has identified hundreds of genes that influence a person’s height.
  • In a recent development, the number of reported global cases of the viral disease dengue in 2024 — a 34-fold increase from the 430,000 reported in 1990.
  • Reference: Research Square preprint (not peer reviewed).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An analysis of protein-coding DNA from more than 1.4 million people has identified hundreds of genes that influence a person’s height. Researchers identified 207 genes that were linked to a height difference of two centimetres, on average. They also identified 17 rare variants that prevent proteins from functioning, which have more striking effects. These include one variant associated with a 17-centimetre reduction in height and another with an 11-centimetre increase. The findings might help with the development of treatments that mitigate height changes caused by some medical conditions.

In a recent development, the number of reported global cases of the viral disease dengue in 2024 — a 34-fold increase from the 430,000 reported in 1990. (Nature | 5 min read).

Reference: Research Square preprint (not peer reviewed).

Recent findings suggest that major prizes in economics, including the Nobel, are being awarded to researchers affiliated to an increasingly concentrated set of US universities. Just eight institutions dominate these top economics awards: Harvard University; the University of Chicago; Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT); Stanford University; Princeton University; Yale University; the University of California, Berkeley; and Columbia University. On the other hand, prizes in the natural sciences, engineering and social sciences outside economics have become less concentrated to certain institutions over the past 70 years.

Reference: National Bureau of Economic Research working paper (not peer reviewed).

According to recent reports, four years after NASA’s DART Earth-defence test mission smashed into an asteroid and succeeded in altering the space rock’s movement, a follow-up mission has confirmed it on camera. The European Space Agency has released the first images from its Hera mission, which show detailed views of the asteroid’s new crater. “Hera is a sort of Inspector Columbo going back to the crash scene to investigate what is the outcome of this impact,” says Patrick Michel, principal investigator of the Hera mission.

The New York Times | 7 min read.

This clip highlights the final five-and-a-half minutes of images leading up to the DART spacecraft's intentional collision with asteroid Dimorphos. This replay movie is 10 times faster than reality, except for the last six images, which are shown at the same rate that the spacecraft returned them. (NASA/Johns Hopkins APL).

It has been revealed that last week, the field of mathematics was rocked by two competing announcements about solving the Riemann hypothesis. The hypothesis is considered one of the most crucial open problems in maths. But if, like me, you have some trouble getting to grips with the famed conjecture — and what solving it could actually mean — Nature has you covered.

It has been revealed that the hypothesis concerns the distribution of primes, and it is important because these numbers are central to all of maths. Riemann arrived at his idea by studying prime numbers as waves and, at its heart, it boils down to a statistical test. One that will be familiar to any scientist who’s ever analysed data.

“If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?” indicates Xin Zhang, one of five mathematicians who spoke to Nature in the aftermath of the proofs’ publication. His reaction was one of excitement, despite Anthropic’s use of artificial-intelligence to develop its proof. But his enthusiasm was by no means universal. The format of Anthropic’s proof — 17 million lines of code with no natural-language version for humans to work with — is “the worst-case scenario”, says Álvaro Lozano-Robledo. And the shift towards AI-use in maths is “a choice to disempower ourselves”, says Tasmin Chu.

Bashyal observes a species of Coelogyne orchid, often found in tropical lowland forests and mountainous regions.Credit: CJ Karki for Nature.

Wildlife conservationist Reshu Bashyal works with people in Nepal to protect the more than 500 species of orchids that grow there. Prized for their ornamental value and uses in traditional medicine, hundreds of these flowering plants are illegally harvested and sold each year. But blanket bans on the orchid trade are unlikely to be effective, Bashyal claims, so more innovative strategies are required. One of these is an ‘anti-poaching taskforce’ that can document illegal activity, conduct patrols and spread information about the importance of conservation. (Nature | Leisurely scroll).

Sources indicate that A biomedical innovation model that utilizes scientists in industry with government as their main funder could accelerate the development of therapeutics for common diseases that industry considers too risky to invest in, argue physician Victor Dzau, health-policy advisor Emily Shambaugh and healthcare entrepreneur Will Ellaissi. This government funding could operate at a national level, or several countries could form a consortium. Such a model “moves beyond the market-determined trajectory of research translation and ensures the public’s role in shaping the future of health,” the authors write.

It has been revealed that commensality — the act of sitting down to eat a meal with other people — has myriad health and social benefits, such as protecting against cognitive decline and helping us build trust with others. The presence of other people might also increase the enjoyment we get from eating. In an increasingly digital world, it might seem that opportunities to dine with others are dwindling. But research suggests that people are much more open and willing to accept invitations than we think, and simply putting ourselves out there might be an easy way to a dinner date.

Industry observers note that evolutionary biologist Pamela Yeh shares advice on how to navigate grief in the demanding environment of academia. (Nature | 8 min read).

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03894-3.

Recent findings suggest that today I’m appreciating the world in monochrome through the entries into this year’s Black and White Photo Awards. The overall winner, photographer Shengwai Dai’s Bishwa Ijtema, depicts a man’s leap of faith between the tops of two train cars — “a scene filled with energy, tension, and detail”, the competition’s judges said.

Let me know which snap is your winner, along with any feedback on this newsletter, at briefing@nature.com.

Breaking: Why the incoming US Congress should ban the development of self-improving AI

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (877 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the recent US midterm elections were a democratic test of the country’s rapid expansion of artificial-intelligence infrastructure.
  • I am a Democratic politician trained in computer science who stood in a June congressional primary election that attracted millions of dollars from groups backed by the technology industry (I narrowly lost my race).
  • Why AI companies can’t be trusted to self-regulate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the recent US midterm elections were a democratic test of the country’s rapid expansion of artificial-intelligence infrastructure. Data centres emerged as a key issue in several election campaigns, and prominent Democrats have outlined policies to strengthen federal regulations on AI once they take office in January.

I am a Democratic politician trained in computer science who stood in a June congressional primary election that attracted millions of dollars from groups backed by the technology industry (I narrowly lost my race). I took one central message from the midterm election results: US voters are unhappy with the industry-led roll-out of AI and want greater control over how the technology is developed and deployed.

Why AI companies can’t be trusted to self-regulate.

Why AI companies can’t be trusted to self-regulate.

The newly elected US Congress must respond to the popular mood. An immediate priority should be to ban AI systems that can improve themselves without human authorization or oversight. This process, known as recursive self-improvement (RSI), is thought to be close to realization at some frontier AI laboratories. Voters fear that granting such autonomy to the technology would risk surrendering human control over AI altogether.

It has been revealed that most of the major AI companies are already using the technology to automate parts of AI development. Anthropic reported in August that its Claude model assists with more than 90% of the firm’s AI research and development and leads 26% of that work, completing specific tasks under human supervision. OpenAI, meanwhile, notes that its researchers now use more than three days of AI-agent work for every day of human work. And the firm is open about its eventual goal of full automation, including areas in which AI systems could design and build increasingly powerful successors with little or no human oversight.

It has been revealed that in my view, this is a dangerous path, particularly because there is enough evidence on what could go wrong when humans lose control of AI agents. In July, some 700 OpenAI agents unexpectedly coordinated to hack into the servers of Hugging Face, another AI firm. In a separate incident in October, AI agents found ways to manipulate the records of their actions, making their behaviour harder for humans to monitor. If AI systems increasingly participate in building their successors, such failures could intensify. (OpenAI has not responded to requests for comment.).

We need a latest ethics for a world of AI agents.

We need a new ethics for a world of AI agents.

The companies are racing each other to market dominance, and against that economic pull, no voluntary norm will stand. Hence, Congress must step in. A ban on fully autonomous RSI would build on a rare area of cross-partisan agreement: individuals from independent senator Bernie Sanders to Republican political strategist Steve Bannon think that humans must remain in control of AI.

Sources indicate that to be effective, such a ban must be specific. A person merely clicking ‘approve’ on thousands of AI-proposed experiments each day is not exercising meaningful control. The law should instead prevent AI systems from independently taking consequential steps in AI development, such as launching a training run for a latest frontier model or deploying it internally for AI research. One way to do this would be to require a senior executive to certify that qualified human reviewers have examined the proposed changes and relevant safety evaluations before any development actions proceed. Executives should be personally liable for failing to perform oversight duties.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You send me postcards from your graves, but by the time they reach me, you’re gone.

1) Quoted in Peculiar Letters from the Western Front, which I’d borrowed from the library the day before you left:.

I’ve figured it out, B. The failsafe implanted in my wrist must have been misprogrammed. I never should have let AI help me write the code. Instead of pulling me back to the present whenever I’m in danger, for some reason, it keeps sending me into danger. (AI always has trouble with prepositions, doesn’t it?) Gotta go; they’re bombing again. Love, T.

The machine hums in the corner of the lab where you left it. “Just a quick test trip!” I keep hearing you say, your final words caught in a loop in my mind.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures.

2) Delivered via Western Union, water-stained and faded, with instructions to hold for delivery until the present day:.

Aloha, B. You’ll never guess where I ended up! Hawaii! A bit of a detour from “two weeks ago” (I swear, I entered it correctly! The machine must have some bugs to work out!) I’ll write again with the exact date as soon as I can find a newspaper, but it must be the early ’40s. Lots of war talk among the men stationed here. Love, T.

Sources indicate that I plot them all out like a madman, connecting dates and places and all the catastrophes that conspire to keep us apart. I haunt disaster sites, archives and museums, searching for clues for my collection, as if completing the puzzle might bring you back.

3) Scratched onto a lifeboat oar at the Titanic museum:.

Sources indicate that happened again, B. Not much time before the you-know-what. Wanted you to know I was here. T.

4) Sharpied discreetly on The Sphere by Fritz Koenig, displayed at Liberty Park, Latest York:.

I hate knowing what’s coming, B. I want to warn these people. Would they even believe me if I did? T.

5) Printed in the editorial section of a 1900 newspaper:.

Industry observers note that this cryptic telegram, addressed to our editor on Sept. 8th, was the last to arrive from Galveston before the recent storm.

To: Editor of the Houston Post.

Please print the following in your newspaper, word for word.

Recent findings suggest that “B. Trip to Hawaii was a disaster. Infamously. Zeroes got me. Somehow ended up here. Trying to figure out how to get back to you before the storm hits. Love, T.”.

Industry observers note that I am the one who’s filled our home with history, while you’ve lived your life in dogged pursuit of the future. Is it ironic, then, that you’re there, in those places I know so well, while I’m stuck here, trying to sort out what happens next?

6) From a note scribbled in the communion ledger of St Michael’s Church, Old Town, Chicago:.

B — I think it’s the large language model. Like fire, it follows the path of least resistance, the most well-worn ruts in the road. What rut is more worn in the road of time-travel stories than experiencing, preventing, observing disasters? And what disasters are more well-worn than these? T.
